objective_text: Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
question_text: At which OSI layer does a standard Ethernet switch primarily use MAC addresses to forward frames?
answer_b: Network
answer_c: Transport
answer_d: Session
correct_explanation: The data link layer handles frames and uses MAC addresses for local network forwarding. A standard Layer 2 switch builds a MAC address table and forwards frames according to that table.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The data link layer is responsible for frames and MAC-address-based forwarding.
answer_b_explanation: The network layer uses logical addressing, such as IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and selects routes between networks.
answer_c_explanation: The transport layer provides end-to-end transport functions through protocols such as TCP and UDP.
answer_d_explanation: The session layer manages communication sessions and does not perform Ethernet frame forwarding.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.1 associates MAC addresses and switching with Layer 2. IEEE 802.3 defines Ethernet framing and media access.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
question_text: A public web application runs on four identical servers. One server is overloaded while the others are lightly used. The company wants a device that can distribute new HTTPS connections and stop sending traffic to a failed server. Which appliance best meets the requirement?
answer_b: Load balancer
answer_c: Network-attached storage appliance
answer_d: Wireless LAN controller
correct_explanation: A load balancer distributes client connections across multiple application servers and can use health checks to remove an unavailable server from service.
answer_a_explanation: A router forwards traffic between IP networks, but basic routing does not provide application-server health checks and connection distribution across a server pool.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A load balancer distributes sessions and can monitor server health before forwarding new connections.
answer_c_explanation: A network-attached storage appliance provides file storage rather than distributing application connections.
answer_d_explanation: A wireless LAN controller manages wireless access points and related radio or client settings.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.2 includes load balancers and their network functions.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
question_text: Which statement best distinguishes cloud elasticity from scalability?
answer_a: Elasticity changes data formats, while scalability changes network protocols.
answer_b: Elasticity applies only to storage, while scalability applies only to compute resources.
answer_c: Elasticity adjusts resources as demand changes, while scalability is the broader ability to increase or decrease capacity.
answer_d: Elasticity is limited to private clouds, while scalability is limited to public clouds.
correct_explanation: Elasticity is the ability to add or remove resources in response to changing demand, often automatically. Scalability is the broader capability of a system to handle growth or reduction by changing available capacity.
answer_a_explanation: The distinction is not based on data formats or network protocols.
answer_b_explanation: Both elasticity and scalability can apply to compute, storage, and other cloud resources.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Elasticity focuses on responsive resource adjustment, while scalability describes the ability to change capacity.
answer_d_explanation: Both concepts can apply to public, private, and hybrid cloud environments.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.3 explicitly includes scalability and elasticity.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
question_text: A network engineer is documenting standard DNS traffic. Which TWO statements are correct?
answer_a: DNS commonly uses UDP port 53 for routine queries.
answer_b: DNS uses TCP port 25 for zone transfers.
answer_c: DNS switches to ICMP when a response is too large for UDP.
answer_d: DNS can use TCP port 53, including for zone transfers and some larger responses.
correct_explanation: Standard DNS uses port 53. Routine queries commonly use UDP, while TCP port 53 is used for operations such as zone transfers and can be used when a response requires TCP.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. UDP port 53 is commonly used for ordinary DNS queries and responses.
answer_b_explanation: TCP port 25 is assigned to SMTP. DNS zone transfers use TCP port 53.
answer_c_explanation: DNS does not use ICMP as its fallback transport. TCP can be used when UDP is not suitable.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. TCP port 53 supports DNS operations including zone transfers and responses that use TCP.
reference_notes: IANA assigns domain service to TCP and UDP port 53. RFC 1035 describes DNS use of UDP and TCP.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers.
question_text: Two buildings are connected by an existing 8 km single-mode fiber path. The network team needs a 10 Gbps Ethernet link. Which transceiver type is the most appropriate choice?
answer_b: 1000BASE-T
answer_c: DOCSIS cable modem
answer_d: 10GBASE-LR
correct_explanation: 10GBASE-LR is designed for 10 Gigabit Ethernet over single-mode fiber and supports distances suitable for an 8 km building-to-building link when the installed fiber and optical budget meet the standard.
answer_a_explanation: 10GBASE-SR is intended for short-range links over multimode fiber, not an 8 km single-mode path.
answer_b_explanation: 1000BASE-T provides 1 Gbps over balanced copper cabling and does not meet the speed or media requirement.
answer_c_explanation: A DOCSIS cable modem is used for cable-provider access networks rather than a point-to-point enterprise fiber link.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. 10GBASE-LR is a long-reach 10 Gbps option for single-mode fiber.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.3 defines 10 Gigabit Ethernet optical variants, including long-reach operation over single-mode fiber.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use appropriate IPv4 network addressing.
question_text: A subnet is assigned 192.168.50.64/27. Which address range can be assigned to hosts in this subnet?
correct_explanation: A /27 prefix leaves 5 host bits, so the subnet contains 32 addresses. This block begins at 192.168.50.64 and ends at 192.168.50.95. The first address is the network address and the last is the directed broadcast address, leaving 192.168.50.65 through 192.168.50.94 for hosts.
answer_a_explanation: This range includes the network address and broadcast address, which are not assignable to ordinary hosts.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Removing the .64 network address and .95 broadcast address leaves .65 through .94.
answer_c_explanation: This range incorrectly removes two additional usable host addresses.
answer_d_explanation: This range includes .95, which is the directed broadcast address for the /27 subnet.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: /27 gives 32 addresses. Network 192.168.50.64, broadcast 192.168.50.95, usable hosts .65 through .94.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for automatic failover while preserving the primary route during normal operation.
question_text: A branch router learns 10.50.0.0/16 through OSPF over its primary WAN link. A second WAN link should carry traffic to that network only when the OSPF route is unavailable. Which configuration best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Configure the backup static route with a lower administrative distance than the OSPF route.
answer_b: Remove OSPF and use equal-cost default routes on both WAN links.
answer_c: Configure a static route to 10.50.0.0/16 with an administrative distance higher than the OSPF route.
answer_d: Configure a host route for the OSPF neighbor address through the backup WAN link.
correct_explanation: A floating static route uses a higher administrative distance than the preferred dynamic route. The router installs the OSPF route during normal operation and can install the higher-distance static route when the OSPF route is withdrawn.
answer_a_explanation: A lower administrative distance would make the backup static route preferred during normal operation.
answer_b_explanation: Removing OSPF changes the primary routing design and equal-cost defaults do not specifically provide the requested backup route to 10.50.0.0/16.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A higher-distance static route remains inactive while the OSPF route exists and becomes available after the preferred route is lost.
answer_d_explanation: A host route to the neighbor does not provide a backup route for the entire 10.50.0.0/16 destination network.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.1 includes static and dynamic routing, administrative distance, and route selection. RFC 2328 is the primary OSPFv2 specification.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Two switches are connected by an 802.1Q trunk. Logs report a native VLAN mismatch, and untagged management frames are being placed into different VLANs at each end. Which change should the administrator make?
answer_a: Set one switch port to half duplex.
answer_b: Disable spanning tree on the trunk.
answer_c: Increase the trunk MTU on only one switch.
answer_d: Configure the same native VLAN on both ends of the trunk.
correct_explanation: Both ends of an 802.1Q trunk should agree on the native VLAN so untagged frames are classified consistently. Matching the native VLAN settings addresses the reported mismatch.
answer_a_explanation: Changing duplex does not correct inconsistent VLAN classification and may introduce a separate performance problem.
answer_b_explanation: Disabling spanning tree does not correct the mismatch and can increase the risk of a Layer 2 loop.
answer_c_explanation: A one-sided MTU change can create frame-size problems and does not align the native VLAN settings.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Matching the native VLAN on both trunk endpoints ensures consistent handling of untagged frames.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1Q defines VLAN tagging and bridged network behavior. CompTIA objective 2.2 includes native VLANs and 802.1Q tagging.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_text: Which characteristic is generally associated with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi when compared with 5 GHz Wi-Fi?
answer_a: Longer range and better obstacle penetration, but fewer non-overlapping channels
answer_b: Shorter range and more available spectrum in every regulatory domain
answer_c: A requirement to use WPA3 for every connection
answer_d: Support for ad hoc networks but not infrastructure networks
correct_explanation: The lower 2.4 GHz frequency generally provides better propagation and obstacle penetration than 5 GHz, but the band has less usable spectrum and fewer non-overlapping channel choices.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. This describes the common range and channel-planning tradeoff between the two bands.
answer_b_explanation: 2.4 GHz generally has longer, not shorter, range. Spectrum availability also depends on the regulatory domain.
answer_c_explanation: Security requirements are not determined solely by using the 2.4 GHz band.
answer_d_explanation: Both frequency bands can support infrastructure networking when the wireless standard and equipment permit it.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 covers wireless frequency options, channel characteristics, and channel widths.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
question_text: Which device supplies temporary battery power to network equipment during a brief utility outage?
answer_b: Uninterruptible power supply
answer_c: Passive power distribution unit
answer_d: Equipment rack
correct_explanation: An uninterruptible power supply provides battery-backed power for a limited period, allowing equipment to remain online during a short outage or to shut down in a controlled manner.
answer_a_explanation: A patch panel organizes and terminates cabling but does not provide electrical power.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A UPS provides temporary battery-backed power.
answer_c_explanation: A passive PDU distributes available power to equipment but does not provide battery runtime.
answer_d_explanation: A rack physically mounts equipment but does not supply backup power.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.4 includes UPS and power-distribution considerations for physical installations.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Two switches have two available 1 Gbps Ethernet links between them. The network team wants increased aggregate capacity and link redundancy without spanning tree blocking one of the links. Which feature should be configured?
answer_b: 802.1X authentication
answer_c: LACP link aggregation
answer_d: Native VLAN tagging
correct_explanation: LACP can combine compatible physical links into one logical link. Traffic can be distributed across members, and the logical connection can remain available when one member fails.
answer_a_explanation: Port mirroring copies traffic to a monitoring interface and does not combine links for forwarding.
answer_b_explanation: 802.1X controls network access and does not aggregate inter-switch links.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. LACP forms a link aggregation group that provides aggregate capacity and member-link redundancy.
answer_d_explanation: The native VLAN setting controls handling of untagged frames and does not combine physical links.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1AX defines link aggregation. CompTIA objective 2.2 includes link aggregation and LACP.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
question_text: An undocumented switch configuration change caused an outage, and the operations team could not quickly determine what had changed. Which process improvement would best reduce the chance and impact of a similar event?
answer_a: Delete older network diagrams after each maintenance window.
answer_b: Permit emergency changes without recording the final configuration.
answer_c: Rely on the technician who made the change to remember the previous settings.
answer_d: Require an approved change record with a configuration baseline, implementation steps, and a backout plan.
correct_explanation: A documented change process provides authorization, records the intended modification, preserves a known baseline, and defines how to reverse the change if validation fails.
answer_a_explanation: Removing older documentation reduces the information available for comparison and recovery.
answer_b_explanation: Emergency work may require an expedited process, but the final change and resulting configuration should still be recorded.
answer_c_explanation: Personal memory is not a reliable substitute for a controlled configuration record.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Approval, baselines, implementation details, and backout procedures support controlled change and faster recovery.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.1 includes change management, production configuration, backup configuration, and baselines.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: Users report intermittent packet loss between an application server and its default gateway. The managed switch supports traffic monitoring features. Which action will let an analyst inspect copies of the affected Ethernet frames without moving the server connection?
answer_a: Mirror the server port to a packet-analysis port.
answer_b: Lower the DNS time-to-live value.
answer_c: Add a static default route to the application server.
answer_d: Disable SNMP polling on the switch.
correct_explanation: Port mirroring copies frames from a monitored interface or VLAN to an analyzer interface. A packet analyzer connected to the destination port can inspect the traffic while the original link remains in service.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Port mirroring supplies a copy of the relevant frames to a packet analyzer.
answer_b_explanation: DNS TTL affects caching of name records and does not expose the packet-level cause of loss between the server and gateway.
answer_c_explanation: A static route is not a monitoring method and may alter traffic before the cause is understood.
answer_d_explanation: Disabling SNMP removes monitoring data and does not provide frame contents.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.2 includes port mirroring and packet capture as network monitoring technologies.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
question_text: A service has a recovery point objective of 15 minutes and a recovery time objective of 4 hours. Which statement correctly interprets these targets?
answer_a: The service must run for 15 minutes before each backup and may lose 4 hours of data.
answer_b: The recovery design targets no more than 15 minutes of data loss and restoration of service within 4 hours.
answer_c: The service must be repaired in 15 minutes and tested every 4 hours.
answer_d: The backup site must be 15 minutes away and remain active for 4 hours.
correct_explanation: RPO describes the acceptable amount of data loss measured backward in time, while RTO describes the target duration for restoring the service after disruption. Here, the design targets at most 15 minutes of lost data and service recovery within 4 hours.
answer_a_explanation: This reverses the meaning of the two objectives and treats them as backup scheduling rules.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. The RPO limits target data loss, and the RTO limits target restoration time.
answer_c_explanation: RPO is not repair time, and RTO is not a testing frequency.
answer_d_explanation: Neither objective specifies the physical distance to a recovery site.
reference_notes: NIST contingency-planning guidance defines recovery objectives and planning concepts. CompTIA objective 3.3 includes RPO and RTO.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
question_text: A company is publishing email-delivery information and reverse-lookup information in DNS. Which TWO record types should the administrator configure?
answer_a: CNAME record to identify the receiving mail exchanger
answer_b: MX record to identify the receiving mail exchanger
answer_c: PTR record to map an IP address to a host name for reverse lookup
answer_d: TXT record to map an IP address to a host name for reverse lookup
correct_explanation: An MX record identifies the mail exchanger responsible for receiving email for a domain. A PTR record supports reverse DNS by mapping an address in the reverse namespace to a host name.
answer_a_explanation: A CNAME creates an alias for another canonical name. It is not the record used to publish a domain's mail exchanger.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. MX records identify mail exchangers and include preference values.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. PTR records are used for reverse address-to-name mappings.
answer_d_explanation: TXT records hold arbitrary text and are not the standard reverse-lookup mapping record.
reference_notes: RFC 1034 and RFC 1035 define DNS concepts and record behavior, including MX and PTR records.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Which comparison between RADIUS and TACACS+ is correct?
answer_a: RADIUS uses TCP port 49, while TACACS+ uses UDP port 1812.
answer_b: RADIUS is limited to wireless clients, while TACACS+ is limited to site-to-site VPNs.
answer_c: RADIUS commonly uses UDP and often combines authentication with authorization, while TACACS+ uses TCP and separates the AAA functions.
answer_d: Both protocols transmit the complete authentication exchange as unprotected cleartext.
correct_explanation: RADIUS commonly uses UDP for authentication and accounting and often combines authentication and authorization information. TACACS+ uses TCP and supports separate authentication, authorization, and accounting exchanges.
answer_a_explanation: The transports and ports are reversed. TACACS+ uses TCP port 49, while RADIUS commonly uses UDP ports such as 1812 and 1813.
answer_b_explanation: Both protocols can support multiple access scenarios and are not restricted to the listed uses.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. This describes a key operational distinction between the two AAA protocols.
answer_d_explanation: The protocols provide protection for authentication information, although their protection models differ.
reference_notes: RFC 2865 specifies RADIUS. RFC 8907 specifies TACACS+ and its separate AAA exchanges.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: Several users on the same LAN are unexpectedly sending traffic through an unknown workstation. Their ARP caches show the default gateway IP address mapped to the workstation's MAC address. Which attack is most likely occurring?
answer_b: VLAN pruning
answer_c: Password spraying
answer_d: ARP poisoning
correct_explanation: ARP poisoning sends misleading ARP information so systems associate a legitimate IP address, such as the default gateway, with an attacker-controlled MAC address. This can place the attacker in the traffic path.
answer_a_explanation: DNS amplification is a reflection-based denial-of-service technique and does not explain the altered local ARP mappings.
answer_b_explanation: VLAN pruning controls which VLANs traverse a trunk and does not poison host ARP caches.
answer_c_explanation: Password spraying attempts a small number of passwords against many accounts and does not alter IP-to-MAC mappings.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The gateway IP has been falsely associated with the attacker's MAC address through ARP poisoning.
reference_notes: RFC 826 defines ARP operation. CompTIA objective 4.2 includes ARP poisoning and spoofing.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for enforcing authenticated access and isolating noncompliant endpoints.
question_text: A company wants every wired switch port to require user or device credentials before granting normal network access. Endpoints that fail a compliance check should be placed in a restricted remediation VLAN. Which solution best meets the requirement?
answer_a: 802.1X port-based authentication integrated with NAC and a RADIUS server
answer_b: A static MAC-address allowlist maintained independently on every access switch
answer_c: A single untagged VLAN configured on all access ports without authentication
answer_d: Port mirroring from every access port to a packet-capture appliance
correct_explanation: 802.1X controls access at the switch port, RADIUS provides centralized authentication services, and NAC can evaluate endpoint posture and assign an appropriate access policy or remediation VLAN.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The combined solution authenticates the connection and can apply a restricted policy to noncompliant endpoints.
answer_b_explanation: Static MAC filtering is difficult to manage at scale, MAC addresses can be spoofed, and it does not perform the requested credential and posture checks.
answer_c_explanation: An unauthenticated VLAN does not verify users or devices and does not distinguish compliant from noncompliant endpoints.
answer_d_explanation: Port mirroring supports monitoring but does not enforce admission or assign remediation access.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1X defines port-based network access control. RADIUS can provide centralized authentication. CompTIA objective 4.3 includes NAC, 802.1X, and VLAN assignment.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
question_text: After a technician develops a likely theory for the cause of a network problem, what is the next step in the troubleshooting methodology?
answer_a: Document the findings and lessons learned.
answer_b: Test the theory to determine the cause.
answer_c: Establish a plan of action and identify potential effects.
answer_d: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures.
correct_explanation: After establishing a theory of probable cause, the technician tests the theory. A confirmed theory supports planning and implementing a correction. An unconfirmed theory leads to a new theory or escalation.
answer_a_explanation: Documentation occurs after resolution and verification.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. The next step is to test the proposed cause.
answer_c_explanation: A plan of action follows confirmation of the cause.
answer_d_explanation: Verification and preventive measures follow implementation of the solution.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.1 lists the troubleshooting methodology in sequence.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A new 10 Gbps fiber link remains down. One switch uses a 10GBASE-SR transceiver, the other uses a 10GBASE-LR transceiver, and the installed cable is single-mode fiber. Which issue should the technician correct first?
answer_b: An exhausted DHCP address pool
answer_c: The incompatible transceiver and fiber combination
answer_d: A route-summary statement on the core router
correct_explanation: Both ends of a fiber link must use compatible optical standards, wavelengths, and media. SR and LR optics are different physical-layer variants, and SR is not the appropriate optic for the stated single-mode path.
answer_a_explanation: DNS records do not determine whether the physical fiber interface establishes a link.
answer_b_explanation: DHCP address availability affects client addressing after link establishment, not optical carrier compatibility.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The optics and installed fiber must be matched at both ends before higher-layer troubleshooting.
answer_d_explanation: Routing configuration does not prevent the physical optical interface from detecting a compatible link.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.3 defines distinct Ethernet optical variants. CompTIA objective 5.2 includes transceiver mismatch and signal issues.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: A workstation is configured as 192.168.40.70/26 with default gateway 192.168.40.1. It can communicate with 192.168.40.65 but cannot reach any remote network. Which configuration issue best explains the symptoms?
answer_a: The workstation has no DNS search suffix.
answer_b: The workstation and gateway use duplicate MAC addresses.
answer_c: The DHCP lease duration is too short.
answer_d: The default gateway address is outside the workstation's local /26 subnet.
correct_explanation: A /26 has blocks of 64 addresses. The workstation address 192.168.40.70 belongs to 192.168.40.64/26, whose usable range is 192.168.40.65 through 192.168.40.126. The configured gateway 192.168.40.1 belongs to 192.168.40.0/26, so the workstation cannot reach it directly as a local gateway.
answer_a_explanation: A DNS search suffix affects name completion but does not prevent IP routing to remote networks.
answer_b_explanation: A duplicate MAC address could cause local instability, but the addresses shown directly identify a subnet and gateway mismatch.
answer_c_explanation: The workstation already has a valid address and local connectivity, so lease duration does not explain the unreachable gateway.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The host is in 192.168.40.64/26, while 192.168.40.1 is in a different /26 subnet.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 192.168.40.70/26 is in 192.168.40.64 through .127. Usable addresses are .65 through .126. Gateway .1 is outside that subnet.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: A small office has four nearby 2.4 GHz access points configured on channels 1, 4, 8, and 11. Users report high retransmission rates and inconsistent throughput. Which change is the best first step?
answer_a: Redesign the channel plan to use non-overlapping channels such as 1, 6, and 11, and move capable clients to 5 GHz where appropriate.
answer_b: Set every access point to maximum transmit power.
answer_c: Configure 40 MHz channels across the 2.4 GHz band.
answer_d: Assign a different SSID to every access point while retaining the same channels.
correct_explanation: Channels 4 and 8 overlap with nearby 2.4 GHz channels, which can increase contention and retransmissions. A non-overlapping plan and appropriate use of 5 GHz reduce co-channel and adjacent-channel interference.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Channel planning directly addresses the overlap and can improve spectrum use.
answer_b_explanation: Increasing power on every AP can enlarge contention areas and make interference worse.
answer_c_explanation: Wider 2.4 GHz channels consume more of the limited band and can increase overlap.
answer_d_explanation: Changing SSIDs does not remove radio-frequency overlap or contention.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.4 includes channel overlap, interference, and wireless performance. IEEE 802.11 defines wireless LAN operation.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which command-line tool is used to display the sequence of Layer 3 hops toward a destination?
answer_b: traceroute or tracert
answer_c: nslookup
answer_d: cable tester
correct_explanation: Traceroute on many operating systems, or tracert on Windows, sends probes with increasing IP time-to-live values to reveal routers along the path toward a destination.
answer_a_explanation: Ping tests reachability and round-trip response but does not normally list each hop.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Traceroute or tracert reveals the Layer 3 path hop by hop.
answer_c_explanation: Nslookup queries DNS and does not trace the routed path.
answer_d_explanation: A cable tester checks physical cabling and is not a command that discovers routed hops.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.5 includes ping and traceroute. Traceroute behavior relies on IP TTL expiration and ICMP responses.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: Ignoring protocol overhead, how long would it take to transmit 4 GB of data over a 1 Gbps link? Use decimal units: 1 GB equals 1,000,000,000 bytes and 1 Gbps equals 1,000,000,000 bits per second.
answer_b: 8 seconds
answer_c: 32 seconds
answer_d: 40 seconds
correct_explanation: Four gigabytes contains 32 gigabits because each byte contains 8 bits. Dividing 32 gigabits by 1 gigabit per second gives an ideal transmission time of 32 seconds. Real transfer time would be longer because the question excludes protocol and system overhead.
answer_a_explanation: This result treats bytes as bits and omits the factor of 8.
answer_b_explanation: This result does not account for all 4 GB of data at the stated bit rate.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. 4 GB multiplied by 8 equals 32 Gb, and 32 Gb divided by 1 Gbps equals 32 seconds.
answer_d_explanation: This adds time that is not supported by the stated ideal calculation.
reference_notes: Programmatic check using decimal units: 4,000,000,000 bytes multiplied by 8 divided by 1,000,000,000 bits per second equals 32 seconds.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network topologies, architectures, and types.
question_text: A data center carries most of its traffic between servers in different racks. The design should give every rack a consistent number of switch hops to every other rack and allow additional racks to be added predictably. Which architecture best meets these requirements?
answer_a: A three-tier campus design with access, distribution, and core layers
answer_b: A hub-and-spoke WAN with one central router
answer_c: A full mesh in which every server connects directly to every other server
answer_d: A spine-and-leaf fabric in which every leaf switch connects to every spine switch
correct_explanation: A spine-and-leaf fabric provides consistent leaf-to-spine-to-leaf paths for east-west traffic. New server racks can be attached through additional leaf switches with uplinks to the spine layer.
answer_a_explanation: A three-tier design is common in campus networks, but traffic between access blocks can traverse different layers and is less optimized for dense east-west data-center traffic.
answer_b_explanation: Hub-and-spoke centralizes traffic through a hub and does not provide the equal-cost, scalable rack-to-rack fabric described.
answer_c_explanation: A direct full mesh between servers would be operationally and physically impractical as the server count grows.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Each leaf reaches other leaves through the spine layer, creating predictable paths for east-west traffic.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.6 includes spine-and-leaf architecture and east-west traffic patterns.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for application-aware use of multiple WAN connections.
question_text: A company gives each branch an MPLS circuit and a broadband circuit. Voice traffic should automatically use the path with the lowest current latency and jitter, while less-sensitive traffic may use either path. Traffic should fail over when a path degrades. Which solution best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Deploy SD-WAN with application policies and continuous path-performance monitoring.
answer_b: Configure one static default route and leave the second circuit disconnected until an outage.
answer_c: Extend one Layer 2 VLAN across every branch and the data center.
answer_d: Use a local hosts file to select a WAN circuit for each application.
correct_explanation: SD-WAN can measure available underlay paths and steer application flows according to policy and current performance. This supports application-aware selection and automated failover across multiple WAN connections.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. SD-WAN combines centralized policy with monitored underlay paths to steer traffic based on application and performance requirements.
answer_b_explanation: A single active static route does not provide application-aware path selection and requires manual intervention if the unused path is disconnected.
answer_c_explanation: Extending a VLAN does not select among WAN paths according to latency, jitter, or application type.
answer_d_explanation: A hosts file maps names to addresses. It does not control WAN path selection or failover.
reference_notes: MEF 70.2 defines SD-WAN service concepts including application flows, policies, and underlay connectivity. CompTIA objective 1.8 includes SD-WAN.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments.
question_text: Which statement correctly compares VXLAN with a traditional IEEE 802.1Q VLAN?
answer_a: VXLAN removes the need for an IP underlay because it forwards only by physical switch port.
answer_b: VXLAN is limited to the same 12-bit identifier space used by an 802.1Q VLAN tag.
answer_c: VXLAN can encapsulate Layer 2 frames across a Layer 3 underlay and identify logical segments with a VXLAN Network Identifier.
answer_d: VXLAN requires every endpoint to remain in one physical broadcast domain without routing.
correct_explanation: VXLAN creates an overlay by encapsulating Layer 2 traffic for transport across an IP network. A VXLAN Network Identifier identifies the logical segment and provides a larger segmentation space than the VLAN identifier field.
answer_a_explanation: VXLAN depends on an IP underlay to carry encapsulated overlay traffic between tunnel endpoints.
answer_b_explanation: VXLAN uses a 24-bit VNI rather than the 12-bit VLAN identifier field.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. VXLAN overlays logical Layer 2 segments on a routed Layer 3 infrastructure.
answer_d_explanation: VXLAN is used specifically to extend logical segments across a routed underlay rather than requiring one physical broadcast domain.
reference_notes: RFC 7348 defines VXLAN as an overlay for virtualized Layer 2 networks over Layer 3 networks and defines the VXLAN Network Identifier.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
question_text: What is the common name for the protocol data unit at the OSI network layer?
answer_b: Packet
answer_c: Segment
answer_d: Bit
correct_explanation: The network layer uses packets. During encapsulation, a transport-layer segment or datagram is placed inside a network-layer packet, which is then carried inside a data-link frame.
answer_a_explanation: A frame is the data-link-layer protocol data unit.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A packet is the common protocol data unit name at the network layer.
answer_c_explanation: A segment commonly refers to a TCP transport-layer protocol data unit.
answer_d_explanation: Bits represent physical-layer signaling rather than the network-layer protocol data unit.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.1 includes OSI layers, encapsulation, and the associated protocol data units.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
question_text: Which TWO statements correctly describe IP traffic delivery types?
answer_a: Multicast delivers traffic to hosts that have joined a destination group.
answer_b: Broadcast traffic is forwarded across routers to every host on the Internet by default.
answer_c: Unicast sends one packet to all devices in a local broadcast domain.
answer_d: Anycast can advertise the same service address from multiple locations so routing can direct a client to a reachable service instance.
correct_explanation: Multicast targets members of an IP host group. Anycast associates the same service address with multiple service nodes and relies on routing to direct traffic to a reachable instance.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Multicast traffic is addressed to a group and delivered to hosts participating in that group.
answer_b_explanation: Routers generally do not forward local broadcast traffic across routed boundaries by default.
answer_c_explanation: Unicast is one-to-one delivery to a specific destination address, not one-to-all delivery.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Anycast advertises reachability to a shared service address from multiple locations.
reference_notes: RFC 1112 describes IP multicast host groups. RFC 4786 describes operation of services that advertise the same anycast address from multiple nodes.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use appropriate IPv4 network addressing.
question_text: A network administrator must create a subnet for 50 IPv4 hosts from an available /24 network. Which prefix length is the smallest subnet that provides at least 50 usable host addresses under conventional subnetting?
correct_explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits. It contains 64 total addresses, and subtracting the network and broadcast addresses leaves 62 usable host addresses. A /27 provides only 30 usable addresses, so /26 is the smallest suitable choice.
answer_a_explanation: A /28 contains 16 total addresses and 14 conventional usable host addresses.
answer_b_explanation: A /27 contains 32 total addresses and 30 conventional usable host addresses.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A /26 contains 64 total addresses and 62 conventional usable host addresses.
answer_d_explanation: A /25 provides 126 conventional usable host addresses, but it is larger than necessary.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 2^(32-26) equals 64 total addresses and 62 conventional usable host addresses. A /27 provides 30 usable addresses.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: Which routing feature allows many private IPv4 clients to share one public IPv4 address by tracking different transport-layer port numbers?
answer_b: Dynamic routing
answer_c: First-hop redundancy
answer_d: Route aggregation
correct_explanation: Port address translation, often called PAT or NAT overload, distinguishes simultaneous translations by using transport-layer port information. This allows many inside clients to share one public address.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. PAT maps many private address-and-port combinations to one public address using distinct translated ports.
answer_b_explanation: Dynamic routing exchanges reachability information and does not perform address and port translation.
answer_c_explanation: First-hop redundancy provides resilient default-gateway service.
answer_d_explanation: Route aggregation combines multiple network prefixes into a less-specific route.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.1 includes NAT and PAT. RFC 3022 describes traditional NAT and NAPT behavior.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Two switches are connected by two separate trunk links that are not configured as one link aggregation group. When the second link is enabled, users experience a broadcast storm and the MAC address table changes rapidly. Which configuration best preserves link redundancy while preventing the Layer 2 loop?
answer_a: Disable MAC address learning on both switches.
answer_b: Assign the two trunk links to different native VLANs.
answer_c: Configure both links as access ports in the same VLAN.
answer_d: Enable spanning tree so one redundant path can remain in a non-forwarding state.
correct_explanation: Spanning Tree Protocol detects redundant Layer 2 paths and places selected ports into a non-forwarding role. The alternate link remains available to transition if the forwarding path fails.
answer_a_explanation: Disabling MAC learning does not remove the physical loop and would impair normal switching.
answer_b_explanation: Different native VLANs create a mismatch and do not provide loop prevention.
answer_c_explanation: Two access links in the same VLAN would still form a Layer 2 loop.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Spanning tree preserves redundancy while preventing both parallel paths from forwarding simultaneously.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1Q includes bridged-network and spanning-tree behavior. CompTIA objective 2.2 includes STP and trunking.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_text: Which statement best distinguishes WPA3-Personal from WPA2-Personal?
answer_a: WPA3-Personal removes encryption so legacy clients can connect more easily.
answer_b: WPA3-Personal uses Simultaneous Authentication of Equals instead of the WPA2-Personal pre-shared-key authentication exchange.
answer_c: WPA3-Personal requires a RADIUS server for every home and small-office deployment.
answer_d: WPA3-Personal operates only in the 6 GHz frequency band.
correct_explanation: WPA3-Personal uses Simultaneous Authentication of Equals, or SAE, for password-based authentication and key establishment. WPA2-Personal uses the pre-shared-key approach associated with its personal mode.
answer_a_explanation: WPA3-Personal is a protected wireless security mode and does not remove encryption.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. SAE is the defining authentication method used by WPA3-Personal.
answer_c_explanation: RADIUS is associated with enterprise authentication. WPA3-Personal is designed for password-based personal deployments.
answer_d_explanation: WPA3-Personal can be used on supported networks outside the 6 GHz band.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 includes WPA2 and WPA3. SAE is standardized within the IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN specification family.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for reducing recirculation of heated exhaust air.
question_text: Several rack-mounted switches report high inlet temperatures even though the data center's average room temperature is within range. Inspection shows that some racks face opposite directions and heated exhaust air is entering neighboring equipment intakes. Which change best addresses the cause?
answer_a: Increase the humidity set point and leave the rack orientation unchanged.
answer_b: Move all patch panels to the bottom rack units.
answer_c: Arrange rack fronts toward cold aisles and rack backs toward hot aisles, then manage or contain the exhaust path.
answer_d: Replace every copper patch cable with single-mode fiber.
correct_explanation: A hot-aisle and cold-aisle arrangement separates cool intake air from heated exhaust air. Consistent rack orientation and exhaust management reduce recirculation into equipment inlets.
answer_a_explanation: Humidity control matters, but changing humidity does not correct exhaust air entering equipment intakes.
answer_b_explanation: Patch-panel placement does not resolve the airflow direction problem described.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Consistent hot-aisle and cold-aisle orientation addresses the recirculation source.
answer_d_explanation: Changing patch-cable media does not correct rack airflow or exhaust recirculation.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.4 includes airflow, hot and cold aisles, humidity, and temperature considerations for physical installations.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: What is the primary purpose of the virtual IP address used by a first-hop redundancy protocol?
answer_a: It assigns a unique management address to every switch port.
answer_b: It replaces all dynamic routing protocols between routers.
answer_c: It translates private client addresses into public addresses.
answer_d: It gives hosts a stable default-gateway address even when the active router changes.
correct_explanation: A first-hop redundancy group presents a shared virtual router address to hosts. If the active router changes, hosts can continue using the same configured default-gateway address.
answer_a_explanation: Switch ports do not receive unique management addresses from an FHRP virtual IP.
answer_b_explanation: FHRP protects the local default gateway and does not replace routing protocols throughout the network.
answer_c_explanation: Address translation is performed by NAT or PAT rather than by the FHRP virtual address.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The virtual address separates the hosts' gateway configuration from the identity of the currently active router.
reference_notes: RFC 9568 defines a virtual router that can be represented by one or more physical routers. CompTIA objective 2.1 includes FHRP and virtual IPs.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network access and management methods.
question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes out-of-band management from in-band management?
answer_a: Out-of-band management uses a separate management path that may remain reachable when the production data network is impaired.
answer_b: Out-of-band management sends management traffic through the same production interfaces and routes as user traffic.
answer_c: In-band management requires a physical console cable for every session.
answer_d: In-band management can be used only when the managed device has no IP address.
correct_explanation: Out-of-band management uses a separate console, management network, or other independent path. In-band management reaches the device through the production network and therefore depends on that network being available.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The independent path is the central resilience benefit of out-of-band management.
answer_b_explanation: This describes in-band management, where management traffic shares the production network.
answer_c_explanation: In-band methods include IP-based tools such as SSH, HTTPS, and APIs and do not require a console cable.
answer_d_explanation: In-band management normally depends on production IP connectivity to the managed device.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.5 explicitly compares in-band and out-of-band network management methods.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network access and management methods.
question_text: A company is comparing split-tunnel and full-tunnel remote-access VPN configurations. Which TWO statements are correct?
answer_a: A split tunnel sends all Internet and corporate traffic through the organization before any destination is reached.
answer_b: A split tunnel sends traffic for specified corporate networks through the VPN while other traffic can use the client's local connection.
answer_c: A full tunnel prevents the organization from applying security controls to the client's Internet-bound traffic.
answer_d: A full tunnel sends the client's corporate and Internet-bound traffic through the VPN gateway, subject to the configured routing policy.
correct_explanation: Split tunneling routes selected organizational destinations through the VPN and allows other traffic to use the local connection. Full tunneling sends broader client traffic through the VPN gateway so organizational routing and security controls can process it.
answer_a_explanation: This describes full-tunnel behavior rather than split tunneling.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Split tunneling limits VPN routing to designated destinations or traffic.
answer_c_explanation: A full tunnel can increase the organization's ability to inspect and control Internet-bound traffic because that traffic traverses the VPN gateway.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Full tunneling routes both corporate and Internet-bound client traffic through the VPN according to policy.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.5 includes client-to-site VPNs and split versus full tunneling. RFC 4301 provides the IPsec security architecture used by many VPN implementations.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: Which SNMP mechanism allows an agent to send an event notification to a manager without waiting for the next polling interval?
answer_b: Get
answer_c: Trap
answer_d: Set
correct_explanation: An SNMP trap is an unsolicited notification from an agent to a management system. It can report a significant event without requiring the manager to discover it through periodic polling.
answer_a_explanation: A walk retrieves a sequence of managed objects and is initiated by the manager.
answer_b_explanation: A get request is initiated by the manager to read a managed object.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A trap is sent by the agent to report an event asynchronously.
answer_d_explanation: A set operation changes a writable managed object and is initiated by the manager.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.2 includes SNMP traps. RFC 3411 defines the SNMP management framework and notification architecture.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
question_text: Clients in VLAN 20 do not receive IPv4 leases from a centralized DHCP server on another subnet. Clients on the server's local subnet receive leases normally, and routing between the subnets works after clients are given static addresses. Which change should the administrator make on the Layer 3 interface for VLAN 20?
answer_a: Configure the interface as a DNS secondary zone.
answer_b: Configure a DHCP relay address that forwards client requests to the centralized DHCP server.
answer_c: Disable broadcast traffic on the VLAN and remove its default gateway.
answer_d: Configure a static ARP entry for every prospective client.
correct_explanation: Initial DHCP client messages are broadcasts that do not cross a router by themselves. A DHCP relay on the client subnet receives the broadcast and forwards the request to the remote DHCP server.
answer_a_explanation: DNS zone configuration does not forward DHCP lease requests.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A DHCP relay, often configured as a helper address, enables service across routed subnet boundaries.
answer_c_explanation: Removing the gateway would prevent routed connectivity and would not deliver the DHCP request to the remote server.
answer_d_explanation: Static ARP entries do not relay DHCP messages and would be impractical for dynamically addressed clients.
reference_notes: RFC 2131 describes DHCP operation and references relay-agent behavior. RFC 1542 defines BOOTP relay behavior used to forward DHCP messages across routed boundaries.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Help-desk technicians need to reset user passwords and view account status, but they should not create administrators or change firewall policies. Which access-control approach best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Assign a role containing only the password-reset and account-view permissions.
answer_b: Give every technician the same unrestricted administrator account.
answer_c: Share the security administrator's credentials among the help-desk team.
answer_d: Disable authorization checks after each technician completes MFA.
correct_explanation: A narrowly scoped role applies least privilege by granting the permissions required for assigned duties while withholding unrelated administrative capabilities.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The role matches job duties without granting broader security or administrative control.
answer_b_explanation: Unrestricted administrator access exceeds the technicians' stated responsibilities.
answer_c_explanation: Shared privileged credentials weaken accountability and provide excessive access.
answer_d_explanation: MFA verifies identity but does not replace authorization or least-privilege controls.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.1 includes authorization and least privilege. NIST SP 800-207 emphasizes policy-based, least-privilege access decisions.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: Users on one office LAN intermittently receive an unfamiliar default gateway and DNS server. A packet capture shows DHCPOFFER messages from both the authorized server and an employee's small wireless router. What is causing the problem?
answer_b: A DNSSEC validation failure
answer_c: A rogue DHCP server
answer_d: A spanning-tree root election
correct_explanation: The employee router is acting as an unauthorized DHCP server. Clients may accept its offer and receive incorrect network settings, producing intermittent connectivity or traffic redirection.
answer_a_explanation: MAC flooding targets a switch's forwarding table and does not directly issue DHCP configuration offers.
answer_b_explanation: DNSSEC validation affects the authenticity of DNS data and does not assign gateways or DNS server addresses to clients.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The unauthorized device is issuing competing DHCP offers with incorrect configuration values.
answer_d_explanation: A spanning-tree election controls Layer 2 loop prevention and does not generate DHCP leases.
reference_notes: RFC 2131 defines the DHCP offer and lease process. CompTIA objective 4.2 includes rogue DHCP attacks.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_text: A firewall evaluates an ACL from top to bottom and stops at the first matching rule. The ACL currently permits source network 10.20.0.0/16 to an application server. The administrator must block only 10.20.30.0/24 from that server while continuing to allow the rest of 10.20.0.0/16. Which rule change meets the requirement?
answer_a: Place the deny for 10.20.30.0/24 after the existing permit for 10.20.0.0/16.
answer_b: Replace the permit with a deny for the entire 10.20.0.0/16 network.
answer_c: Add an allow rule for 10.20.30.0/24 above the existing permit.
answer_d: Place a deny for 10.20.30.0/24 before the broader permit for 10.20.0.0/16.
correct_explanation: The more-specific deny must appear before the broad permit. Otherwise, traffic from 10.20.30.0/24 matches the /16 permit first and evaluation stops before reaching the deny.
answer_a_explanation: The broad permit would match 10.20.30.0/24 first, so the later deny would not be evaluated.
answer_b_explanation: Denying the entire /16 would block networks that are supposed to remain allowed.
answer_c_explanation: An additional allow rule would not implement the requested block.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The specific exception is evaluated first, and the broader permit then handles the remaining source addresses.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.3 includes ACLs. NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1 discusses ordered firewall policy rules and specific policy requirements.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
question_text: A technician implements a change that appears to resolve a network outage. According to the troubleshooting methodology, what should the technician do next?
answer_b: Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures when appropriate.
answer_c: Develop a new theory without testing the restored service.
answer_d: Replace additional working components to confirm the repair.
correct_explanation: After implementing a solution, the technician should verify that the system and affected services function fully. Appropriate preventive measures can then reduce the chance of recurrence before the work is documented.
answer_a_explanation: The final process includes documenting findings, actions, and outcomes rather than erasing the record.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Verification confirms that the fix restored the expected service and did not leave related problems unresolved.
answer_c_explanation: Developing a new theory is unnecessary when a solution has been implemented and is ready for verification.
answer_d_explanation: Replacing working components introduces risk and is not part of normal post-fix verification.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.1 lists verification of full system functionality and implementation of preventive measures after the solution is implemented.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A switch has a 370 W PoE budget. Twenty-four connected access points each require 18 W during normal operation. Several access points fail to power on even though their Ethernet links and cables test correctly. What is the most likely cause?
answer_a: The requested PoE load exceeds the switch's available power budget.
answer_b: The switch has learned too many MAC addresses.
answer_c: The access points are using overlapping wireless channels.
answer_d: The DHCP lease duration is too long.
correct_explanation: The access points request 24 multiplied by 18 W, which equals 432 W. That exceeds the 370 W PoE budget by 62 W, so the switch cannot supply the requested power to every port.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The aggregate powered-device demand is greater than the switch's PoE budget.
answer_b_explanation: MAC-table capacity affects forwarding and does not explain why powered devices fail to start.
answer_c_explanation: Channel overlap can reduce wireless performance but does not prevent the access points from receiving PoE.
answer_d_explanation: DHCP lease duration affects address assignment timing and does not determine PoE availability.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 24 access points multiplied by 18 W equals 432 W, which is 62 W above the 370 W switch budget.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: Shortly after an unmanaged switch is connected under a desk, broadcast utilization rises sharply, switch CPU usage increases, and the same source MAC addresses repeatedly move between two access ports. Which fault best explains all three symptoms?
answer_b: An incorrect DNS MX record
answer_c: A Layer 2 switching loop
answer_d: A missing default route on the Internet edge router
correct_explanation: A Layer 2 loop can replicate broadcast and unknown-unicast frames continuously. Frames arriving through different loop paths also cause MAC address entries to flap between ports, increasing switch processing load.
answer_a_explanation: An exhausted DHCP pool prevents new leases but does not normally create broadcast replication and MAC flapping between switch ports.
answer_b_explanation: An MX record affects email routing and does not cause the observed Layer 2 symptoms.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Broadcast storms, high switch utilization, and rapidly moving MAC entries are strong indicators of a switching loop.
answer_d_explanation: A missing Internet default route affects external reachability and does not cause local MAC addresses to alternate between access ports.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.3 includes spanning-tree and VLAN issues. IEEE 802.1Q includes loop-prevention behavior for bridged networks.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: Which symptom most directly distinguishes high jitter from consistently high latency on a voice call?
answer_a: Every packet follows the same route to the destination.
answer_b: The link reports a fixed speed and duplex setting.
answer_c: The average one-way delay is high but packet spacing remains steady.
answer_d: Packet arrival intervals vary, causing uneven or choppy audio even when the average delay is acceptable.
correct_explanation: Jitter is variation in packet delay or arrival timing. Real-time audio is sensitive to uneven spacing because the receiver must buffer and play packets at a steady rate.
answer_a_explanation: A consistent route does not define jitter and can exist with either stable or variable delay.
answer_b_explanation: Speed and duplex describe the link configuration rather than variation in packet arrival time.
answer_c_explanation: A consistently high delay describes latency without necessarily indicating high variation.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Variable packet arrival intervals are the defining performance symptom of jitter.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.4 distinguishes latency, packet loss, and jitter as common network performance conditions.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: A technician suspects an open or severe impedance fault inside a copper Ethernet cable run. The technician needs to estimate how far the fault is from the patch panel. Which tool is most appropriate?
answer_b: A time-domain reflectometer
answer_c: A protocol analyzer
answer_d: An optical power meter
correct_explanation: A time-domain reflectometer sends a signal into a copper cable and analyzes reflections. The timing of the reflected signal can estimate the distance to an open, short, or impedance discontinuity.
answer_a_explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer measures wireless spectrum and signal conditions, not the distance to a copper fault.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A TDR is designed to locate cable faults by measuring reflected signal timing.
answer_c_explanation: A protocol analyzer examines network frames and packets but does not measure physical distance to a cable defect.
answer_d_explanation: An optical power meter measures light levels on fiber and is not the proper tool for a copper cable run.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.5 includes time-domain reflectometers and cable-testing tools.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A fiber transmitter outputs -2 dBm. The total estimated loss through the fiber and connectors is 12 dB. The receiver sensitivity is -18 dBm. Ignoring any additional design reserve, what is the calculated receive level and power margin?
answer_a: -14 dBm receive level with 4 dB of positive margin
answer_b: -10 dBm receive level with 2 dB of positive margin
answer_c: -14 dBm receive level that is 4 dB below receiver sensitivity
answer_d: -20 dBm receive level with 16 dB of positive margin
correct_explanation: Subtracting the 12 dB path loss from the -2 dBm transmit level gives -14 dBm at the receiver. The receiver can operate down to -18 dBm, so -14 dBm is 4 dB stronger than the sensitivity threshold, producing 4 dB of positive margin.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. -2 dBm minus 12 dB equals -14 dBm, and -14 dBm minus the -18 dBm threshold equals 4 dB of margin.
answer_b_explanation: The receive level does not follow from subtracting the stated 12 dB loss from -2 dBm.
answer_c_explanation: -14 dBm is 4 dB above, not below, a sensitivity threshold of -18 dBm.
answer_d_explanation: The receive level and stated margin are inconsistent with the given transmit level, loss, and sensitivity.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: -2 dBm minus 12 dB equals -14 dBm. The margin above a -18 dBm sensitivity threshold is 4 dB.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
question_text: A company wants a network security appliance that can inspect traffic and automatically block packets matching a malicious signature before they reach an internal server. Which appliance best meets the requirement?
answer_b: A passive intrusion detection system connected to a mirrored port
answer_c: A forward proxy used by employee web browsers
answer_d: A load balancer distributing requests across application servers
correct_explanation: An inline intrusion prevention system can inspect traffic in the forwarding path and take an active blocking action before malicious packets reach the destination.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. An inline IPS can detect and actively prevent matching traffic from continuing through the network path.
answer_b_explanation: A passive IDS can alert on suspicious traffic but does not sit in the forwarding path to block the packet directly.
answer_c_explanation: A forward proxy intermediates client requests but is not the general-purpose inline signature-blocking control described.
answer_d_explanation: A load balancer distributes application traffic and health-checks servers; it is not primarily an intrusion prevention control.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-94 distinguishes intrusion detection from prevention capabilities and discusses inline network-based prevention.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
question_text: Employees use a provider-hosted email application through a web browser. The provider manages the application, operating systems, and underlying infrastructure. Which cloud service model is being used?
answer_b: Software as a service
answer_c: Platform as a service
answer_d: Private cloud colocation
correct_explanation: Software as a service provides a complete provider-managed application that customers access through a client such as a browser. The customer uses the software without managing the supporting platform or infrastructure.
answer_a_explanation: Infrastructure as a service exposes computing resources while the customer typically manages operating systems and applications.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. The provider delivers and manages the complete application stack.
answer_c_explanation: Platform as a service provides an application-development or deployment platform rather than a finished end-user application.
answer_d_explanation: Colocation describes customer equipment placed in a provider facility and is not one of the defined cloud service models in this scenario.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-145 defines software as a service, platform as a service, and infrastructure as a service.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for applying least-privilege traffic controls between cloud application tiers.
question_text: A cloud application has an Internet-facing load balancer, private application servers, and a private database. The application servers should accept HTTPS only from the load balancer, and the database should accept its database port only from the application servers. Which solution best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Assign one unrestricted security group to every component.
answer_b: Place all components on a public subnet and rely on host names for separation.
answer_c: Use separate security groups for each tier and reference the permitted source tier in the inbound rules.
answer_d: Give every component the same public IP address and filter traffic with DNS records.
correct_explanation: Separate security groups allow each tier to accept only the traffic required from the preceding tier. Referencing the source tier avoids exposing private application and database systems broadly.
answer_a_explanation: A shared unrestricted group would permit more traffic than the application requires.
answer_b_explanation: Public placement and host names do not enforce least-privilege network access between tiers.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Tier-specific security groups can restrict the load balancer, application, and database paths independently.
answer_d_explanation: DNS records do not provide stateful packet filtering, and sharing one public address does not create tier isolation.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.3 includes security groups, security lists, VPCs, and cloud network connectivity. NIST SP 800-207 supports least-privilege policy enforcement.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
question_text: Which protocol normally uses TCP port 22 to provide encrypted command-line access to a network device?
answer_b: SNMP
answer_c: TFTP
answer_d: SSH
correct_explanation: Secure Shell uses TCP port 22 by default and provides encrypted remote-login and command-execution services.
answer_a_explanation: Telnet normally uses TCP port 23 and does not provide the encrypted session requested.
answer_b_explanation: SNMP is used for network monitoring and management data rather than interactive command-line login.
answer_c_explanation: TFTP is a simple file-transfer protocol that normally uses UDP port 69.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. SSH provides encrypted remote command-line access and is assigned TCP port 22.
reference_notes: IANA assigns TCP port 22 to SSH. RFC 4251 defines the SSH protocol architecture.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers.
question_text: Which connector is commonly used as a small-form-factor duplex connector on fiber patch cables?
answer_b: RJ45
answer_c: F-type
answer_d: BNC
correct_explanation: LC is a compact fiber-optic connector commonly paired in a duplex arrangement for transmit and receive fibers.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. LC is a small-form-factor fiber connector commonly used on duplex patch cables and transceivers.
answer_b_explanation: RJ45 is commonly used with twisted-pair copper Ethernet cabling.
answer_c_explanation: F-type is commonly associated with coaxial cabling.
answer_d_explanation: BNC is a bayonet-style connector associated with coaxial applications.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.5 lists LC among fiber connector types and contrasts fiber, twisted-pair, and coaxial media.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network topologies, architectures, and types.
question_text: A small campus has several access switches but does not need separate distribution and core switch layers. The design must still provide redundant high-speed switching and routing between access blocks. Which architecture is most appropriate?
answer_a: A full mesh between every endpoint
answer_b: A collapsed-core architecture
answer_c: A point-to-point serial topology
answer_d: A pure hub-and-spoke design with no redundant central devices
correct_explanation: A collapsed-core design combines the distribution and core functions into one resilient layer. It is commonly suitable when a campus is not large enough to justify separate distribution and core tiers.
answer_a_explanation: A full mesh between endpoints is impractical and does not describe a normal campus hierarchy.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Collapsing distribution and core functions reduces complexity while retaining a resilient aggregation layer.
answer_c_explanation: A single point-to-point serial topology does not aggregate multiple access blocks for a campus.
answer_d_explanation: A nonredundant hub-and-spoke design would not meet the stated resilience requirement.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.6 includes three-tier and collapsed-core network architectures.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments.
question_text: A network team wants every firewall and virtual-network change to be traceable, peer reviewed, repeatable, and easy to restore to a previous approved configuration. Which workflow best supports these goals?
answer_a: Make changes manually in each device interface and keep no configuration history.
answer_b: Store screenshots of each change in a shared folder after deployment.
answer_c: Define the desired configurations as code, store them in version control, and deploy them through an approved automation process.
answer_d: Allow each administrator to maintain a separate undocumented script on a workstation.
correct_explanation: Infrastructure as code stored in version control provides a reviewable change history, repeatable deployments, and a clear path to restore an earlier approved configuration.
answer_a_explanation: Manual changes without history do not provide repeatability, peer review, or reliable rollback.
answer_b_explanation: Screenshots document appearance but do not create a deployable, versioned source of truth.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Versioned configuration definitions and controlled automation support traceability, review, consistency, and rollback.
answer_d_explanation: Separate undocumented scripts create inconsistency and do not provide shared governance or reliable history.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.8 includes infrastructure as code, automation, playbooks and templates, and source-control concepts.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: An enterprise needs an open-standard, link-state routing protocol to exchange routes dynamically between routers inside one organization. Which protocol should it use?
answer_b: ARP
answer_c: VRRP
answer_d: OSPF
correct_explanation: OSPF is an open-standard link-state interior gateway protocol designed to exchange routing information within an autonomous system.
answer_a_explanation: BGP is primarily an interdomain path-vector protocol used between autonomous systems and for policy-based routing.
answer_b_explanation: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to link-layer addresses on a local network and does not exchange routes.
