answer_c_explanation: VRRP provides first-hop default-gateway redundancy rather than dynamic route exchange.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. OSPF is a link-state IGP used within an organization.
reference_notes: RFC 2328 defines OSPF Version 2 as a link-state interior gateway protocol.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for exchanging public routes with two Internet service providers.
question_text: A company owns a public IP prefix and connects to two different ISPs. It must advertise the prefix to both providers and apply routing policy to influence which external paths are preferred. Which solution best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Establish external BGP sessions with both ISPs and apply route policy.
answer_b: Run ARP between the company routers and both ISP networks.
answer_c: Use only a local first-hop redundancy protocol and advertise no routes.
answer_d: Configure a separate DHCP relay for each ISP.
correct_explanation: External BGP is used to exchange reachability information between autonomous systems. Its policy attributes and route-selection process support a multihomed organization advertising its prefix through multiple providers.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. eBGP is the appropriate protocol for exchanging public prefixes and applying interdomain routing policy with separate ISPs.
answer_b_explanation: ARP operates only on a local link and cannot exchange Internet routing information between autonomous systems.
answer_c_explanation: First-hop redundancy protects a local gateway but does not advertise the company's public prefix to external providers.
answer_d_explanation: DHCP relay forwards address-assignment messages and has no role in interdomain route exchange.
reference_notes: RFC 4271 defines BGP-4 route exchange and policy behavior between autonomous systems.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Hosts in VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 are connected to the same multilayer switch. Each VLAN already exists, but the hosts cannot communicate between VLANs. Which configuration is required on the switch?
answer_a: Configure both VLANs as the same native VLAN on every trunk.
answer_b: Create a switched virtual interface for each VLAN, assign gateway addresses, and enable Layer 3 routing.
answer_c: Disable MAC address learning on all access ports.
answer_d: Place every host port into a single link aggregation group.
correct_explanation: A switched virtual interface provides a Layer 3 gateway for its VLAN. Creating an SVI for each VLAN and enabling routing allows the multilayer switch to route traffic between the VLAN subnets.
answer_a_explanation: The native VLAN controls untagged trunk traffic and does not provide Layer 3 routing between VLANs.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. SVIs supply the gateway interfaces required for inter-VLAN routing on a multilayer switch.
answer_c_explanation: Disabling MAC learning would impair normal Layer 2 forwarding and would not add routing.
answer_d_explanation: Link aggregation combines physical links and does not create gateway interfaces for different VLANs.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.2 includes VLANs, switched virtual interfaces, and 802.1Q switching.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: A router has routes for 10.20.8.0/24, 10.20.9.0/24, 10.20.10.0/24, and 10.20.11.0/24. Which single CIDR route summarizes exactly these four contiguous networks?
correct_explanation: Four contiguous /24 networks require two additional host bits, producing a /22 summary. A /22 beginning at the valid boundary 10.20.8.0 covers third-octet values 8 through 11 exactly.
answer_a_explanation: 10.20.0.0/21 covers third-octet values 0 through 7, not the listed networks.
answer_b_explanation: A /23 covers only two /24 networks, such as 10.20.8.0/24 and 10.20.9.0/24.
answer_d_explanation: 10.20.8.0/21 covers eight /24 networks, from third-octet value 8 through 15, so it includes extra networks.
reference_notes: Programmatic verification confirms that 10.20.8.0/22 spans exactly 10.20.8.0 through 10.20.11.255.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_text: Two buildings have clear line of sight and need a dedicated wireless bridge. The installer wants to focus radio energy toward the other building rather than radiating equally in every direction. Which antenna type is most appropriate?
answer_b: Dipole
answer_c: Internal client antenna
answer_d: Directional
correct_explanation: A directional antenna concentrates energy in a defined direction, making it suitable for point-to-point wireless links between known locations.
answer_a_explanation: An omnidirectional antenna distributes energy broadly around the antenna and is less focused for a point-to-point bridge.
answer_b_explanation: A basic dipole commonly provides a broad pattern rather than the focused pattern requested.
answer_c_explanation: A general internal client antenna is not selected specifically to focus a building-to-building link.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. A directional antenna focuses transmit and receive energy toward the remote building.
study_topics: Directional antenna|Point-to-point wireless|Line of sight|Wireless bridge
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 includes antenna types and point-to-point wireless networks.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: Servers in one data-center VLAN use 9000-byte jumbo frames successfully. Traffic to a remote site fails only for large packets with the Don't Fragment bit set, while small packets succeed. One WAN interface still uses a 1500-byte MTU. What is the most likely cause?
answer_b: A duplicate DNS MX record
answer_c: An incorrect spanning-tree root priority
answer_d: An exhausted DHCP lease pool
correct_explanation: The path contains a link that cannot carry the 9000-byte packet. With fragmentation prohibited, large packets fail while smaller packets continue to pass.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The 1500-byte WAN interface creates a smaller path MTU than the jumbo-frame endpoints expect.
answer_b_explanation: An MX record affects email routing and does not selectively drop large IP packets.
answer_c_explanation: Spanning-tree priority affects Layer 2 path selection and does not explain a size-dependent routed-path failure.
answer_d_explanation: DHCP exhaustion affects address assignment rather than established traffic based on packet size.
reference_notes: RFC 1191 describes IPv4 path MTU discovery and handling of packets that exceed a path's supported MTU.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
question_text: Which system is designed to track subnet assignments, reserved addresses, active address usage, and ownership information across an organization?
answer_b: IPAM
answer_c: IDS
answer_d: CDN
correct_explanation: IP address management centralizes information about address spaces, subnets, allocations, reservations, and related ownership or documentation.
answer_a_explanation: A SIEM aggregates and analyzes security and operational event data.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. IPAM is intended to manage and document organizational IP address space.
answer_c_explanation: An IDS detects suspicious activity and does not serve as an address-allocation database.
answer_d_explanation: A CDN distributes cached content closer to users and does not track internal address assignments.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.1 includes IP address management and logical documentation.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: An operations team needs to identify top talkers, source and destination pairs, protocol usage, and traffic volume across a core router without retaining full packet payloads. Which data source is most appropriate?
answer_b: A full packet capture on every access port
answer_c: Exported flow records such as IPFIX
answer_d: A DNS hosts file
correct_explanation: Flow records summarize conversations using fields such as addresses, ports, protocol, counters, and timing. They support traffic-volume and top-talker analysis with less storage than full packet capture.
answer_a_explanation: A rack diagram documents physical placement and contains no live traffic measurements.
answer_b_explanation: Full packet capture can provide payload detail but is more storage-intensive than necessary for the stated flow-level analysis.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. IPFIX is designed to export summarized flow information for traffic analysis.
answer_d_explanation: A hosts file provides static name-to-address mappings and contains no traffic statistics.
reference_notes: RFC 7011 defines IPFIX export of flow information, including traffic counters and identifying fields.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: Routers, switches, and firewalls must send event messages to a centralized platform for correlation and alerting. Which protocol is commonly used to transport these device log messages?
answer_b: LACP
answer_c: SLAAC
answer_d: Syslog
correct_explanation: Syslog provides a standard format and transport framework for event messages generated by network devices and other systems. A centralized collector or SIEM can ingest and correlate those messages.
answer_a_explanation: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to local link-layer addresses and does not transport event logs.
answer_b_explanation: LACP negotiates link aggregation and does not carry device event messages.
answer_c_explanation: SLAAC configures IPv6 addresses and does not provide centralized logging.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Syslog is commonly used to send device-generated event messages to a central log platform.
reference_notes: RFC 5424 defines the syslog protocol and message format.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
question_text: Which TWO statements correctly compare active-active and active-passive high-availability designs?
answer_a: An active-active design can have multiple nodes serving production traffic at the same time.
answer_b: An active-passive design requires the standby node to process the same full production workload continuously.
answer_c: An active-passive design keeps a standby role available to take over when the active role fails.
answer_d: An active-active design removes the need for health checks and failover planning.
correct_explanation: Active-active designs use multiple active service nodes concurrently. Active-passive designs keep one role active while another is prepared to take over following a failure or planned transition.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Active-active architectures distribute service across more than one active node.
answer_b_explanation: A passive standby is not normally serving the same production workload continuously.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The passive role is maintained so it can assume service when the active role becomes unavailable.
answer_d_explanation: Active-active designs still require health checks, state handling, capacity planning, and failure procedures.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.3 includes active-active and active-passive high-availability concepts.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
question_text: A DHCP scope includes addresses 192.168.50.50 through 192.168.50.199, inclusive. Ten addresses are excluded for printers and five are excluded for network devices. How many addresses remain available for dynamic leases?
correct_explanation: The inclusive range contains 199 minus 50 plus 1, which equals 150 addresses. Subtracting 10 printer exclusions and 5 network-device exclusions leaves 135 dynamic addresses.
answer_a_explanation: This subtracts 20 addresses rather than the stated 15 exclusions.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. 150 total addresses minus 15 excluded addresses equals 135 dynamic leases.
answer_c_explanation: This subtracts only 10 exclusions and ignores the five network-device addresses.
answer_d_explanation: This subtracts only five exclusions and ignores the ten printer addresses.
reference_notes: Programmatic verification: (199 - 50 + 1) - 10 - 5 equals 135.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network access and management methods.
question_text: Administrators must manage routers in a restricted network from one hardened system that records sessions and is the only host permitted to initiate management connections into that network. What should the organization deploy?
answer_b: A DHCP relay
answer_c: A wireless controller
answer_d: A jump host
correct_explanation: A jump host is a controlled intermediary used to reach protected systems. It can centralize authentication, access policy, logging, and session monitoring for administrative connections.
answer_a_explanation: A CDN distributes cached content and does not provide a controlled administrative access path.
answer_b_explanation: A DHCP relay forwards address-assignment messages and does not broker management sessions.
answer_c_explanation: A wireless controller manages access points and is not the general privileged-access gateway described.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. A hardened jump host provides a controlled and auditable route into the restricted management network.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.5 includes jump boxes and remote network management methods. NIST SP 800-207 supports controlled policy enforcement for privileged access.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Which PKI component binds a subject's identity information to a public key and is digitally signed by a certificate authority?
answer_b: A symmetric session key
answer_c: A firewall access control list
answer_d: A password hash
correct_explanation: A digital certificate contains a subject's public key and identifying information. A certificate authority's signature allows relying parties to validate that binding through a certification path.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. An X.509 certificate binds identity information to a public key and is signed by an issuing authority.
answer_b_explanation: A symmetric key is shared for encryption and does not provide a CA-signed public identity binding.
answer_c_explanation: An ACL permits or denies traffic and does not certify ownership of a public key.
answer_d_explanation: A password hash is used to verify a password-derived value and is not a public-key identity certificate.
reference_notes: RFC 5280 defines X.509 public-key certificates, certification paths, and certificate authority signatures.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: An attacker places an unauthorized access point near a lobby. It broadcasts the organization's SSID with a stronger signal and presents a fake sign-in page to connected users. Which attack is occurring?
answer_b: MAC flooding
answer_c: Evil twin
answer_d: ARP cache expiration
correct_explanation: An evil-twin attack uses a fraudulent wireless access point that imitates a legitimate network, often with the same SSID, to attract clients and intercept credentials or traffic.
answer_a_explanation: VLAN hopping attempts to gain access to traffic in another VLAN and does not require an impersonating wireless access point.
answer_b_explanation: MAC flooding targets a switch's forwarding table and does not create a fake wireless login portal.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The unauthorized AP imitates the legitimate wireless network to deceive users.
answer_d_explanation: Normal ARP cache expiration does not create an access point or credential-harvesting page.
study_topics: Evil twin|Rogue access point|Wireless attacks|Credential theft
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.2 includes evil-twin and rogue-access-point attacks.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_text: A public web server must accept HTTPS from the Internet, but a compromise of that server should not provide direct access to the internal user network. Where should the server be placed?
answer_a: On the same unrestricted VLAN as employee workstations
answer_b: In a screened subnet separated from both the Internet and the internal network by filtering controls
answer_c: On an unmanaged switch connected directly to the ISP
answer_d: Inside the internal network with all inbound firewall rules disabled
correct_explanation: A screened subnet creates a distinct security zone for public-facing services. Filtering controls can permit required Internet access while restricting traffic between the public server and internal systems.
answer_a_explanation: Placing the public server with employee endpoints would expose the internal network to unnecessary risk.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A screened subnet isolates the Internet-facing service and allows separate inbound and internal access policies.
answer_c_explanation: A direct unmanaged connection would bypass organizational filtering and monitoring controls.
answer_d_explanation: Disabling inbound access would prevent the public service from meeting its stated requirement.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1 discusses firewall policy and screened subnet architectures for public-facing services.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_text: Which TWO actions most directly reduce the attack surface of a newly installed network switch?
answer_a: Enable Telnet so administrators can manage the switch from more devices.
answer_b: Disable unused services and administratively shut down unused interfaces.
answer_c: Configure one shared administrator account for the entire operations team.
answer_d: Replace default credentials and permit encrypted management protocols such as SSH.
correct_explanation: Disabling unused services and ports removes unnecessary exposure. Replacing default credentials and requiring encrypted management reduces the risk of credential abuse and interception.
answer_a_explanation: Telnet transmits session data without the protection provided by SSH and increases management exposure.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Removing unused services and interfaces reduces reachable functionality that could be abused.
answer_c_explanation: A shared administrator account weakens individual accountability and credential control.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Unique protected credentials and encrypted management are core device-hardening measures.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.3 includes changing default credentials, disabling unnecessary ports and services, and using secure protocols.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
question_text: After a network problem is resolved and service is verified, which final troubleshooting step preserves useful information for future incidents?
answer_a: Remove the successful configuration from backup storage.
answer_b: Develop a new theory for the already resolved issue.
answer_c: Document the findings, actions taken, and outcome.
answer_d: Replace additional components that are functioning normally.
correct_explanation: Documenting the symptoms, root cause, corrective actions, and outcome creates an operational record that can improve future troubleshooting and change history.
answer_a_explanation: Removing a known-good backup reduces recovery capability and does not preserve incident knowledge.
answer_b_explanation: A new theory is unnecessary once the issue has been resolved and verified.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Documentation captures what happened and how the problem was corrected.
answer_d_explanation: Replacing working components introduces risk and is not part of closing a resolved incident.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.1 identifies documenting findings, actions, outcomes, and lessons learned as the final troubleshooting step.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: One end of an Ethernet link is forced to 100 Mbps full duplex. The other end is configured for autonegotiation and operates at half duplex. The link remains up, but users report poor performance and the interfaces show collision-related errors. What is the most likely issue?
answer_b: A DNS zone-transfer failure
answer_c: A depleted IPv6 address pool
answer_d: A wireless channel-width conflict
correct_explanation: When one side operates full duplex and the other side operates half duplex, the link can remain active while experiencing collisions, late collisions, frame errors, and severe performance degradation.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The two interfaces are using incompatible duplex modes.
answer_b_explanation: DNS zone transfer affects name-service replication and does not create collision counters on an Ethernet interface.
answer_c_explanation: IPv6 addressing does not explain a link that is up with collision-related physical-interface errors.
answer_d_explanation: Wireless channel settings do not affect duplex negotiation on a wired Ethernet link.
reference_notes: CompTIA objectives 2.2 and 5.2 include speed, duplex, interface status, and error counters.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: A server intermittently loses connectivity. During the outage, an administrator observes that the ARP entry for the server's IPv4 address alternates between two different MAC addresses. Both devices are on the same VLAN. What is the most likely cause?
answer_b: A missing wireless controller
answer_c: An undersized fiber transceiver
answer_d: A duplicate IPv4 address
correct_explanation: If two devices use the same IPv4 address, each may answer ARP requests with its own MAC address. Neighboring systems can repeatedly update the ARP mapping, causing traffic to alternate between the devices.
answer_a_explanation: A CNAME record affects name resolution and does not cause one IPv4 address to map to alternating local MAC addresses.
answer_b_explanation: A wireless controller is unrelated to two wired devices answering for the same IPv4 address.
answer_c_explanation: A transceiver mismatch can disrupt a physical link but does not create competing ARP replies from two MAC addresses.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Two devices claiming the same IPv4 address explain the alternating ARP entries and intermittent reachability.
reference_notes: RFC 826 defines ARP address-to-MAC resolution. CompTIA objective 5.3 includes duplicate IP addresses.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: A branch router can reach all directly connected networks, but it cannot reach any other destination. The routing table contains connected routes only and has no dynamically learned routes. Which configuration is most likely missing?
answer_b: A default route toward the upstream router
answer_c: A second native VLAN on the access switch
answer_d: A local NTP stratum value
correct_explanation: When a router has no specific route to remote destinations, a default route can direct unmatched traffic toward an upstream router that knows the broader network paths.
answer_a_explanation: A PTR record supports reverse DNS lookup and does not add network reachability.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. With only connected routes present, a default route provides a next hop for otherwise unknown destinations.
answer_c_explanation: A native VLAN setting does not populate the branch router's Layer 3 routing table.
answer_d_explanation: NTP stratum relates to time-source distance and does not determine packet forwarding.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.3 includes default routes and route-selection troubleshooting.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: Wireless clients use the same SSID and security settings on several access points. Calls drop when users walk between two areas because the first access point becomes unusable before the second access point has a strong enough signal. What is the best corrective action?
answer_a: Configure different SSIDs on every access point.
answer_b: Reduce both access points to the lowest transmit power without testing.
answer_c: Perform a wireless survey and adjust access-point placement or power to provide appropriate cell overlap.
answer_d: Disable roaming and require users to reconnect manually.
correct_explanation: Roaming depends on usable coverage from the next access point before the current connection degrades too far. A survey can identify the gap and guide placement or power changes that create appropriate overlap.
answer_a_explanation: Different SSIDs would hinder seamless roaming rather than correct the coverage gap.
answer_b_explanation: Reducing power without measurement could make the gap worse.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Survey-driven placement and power adjustments address insufficient overlap between cells.
answer_d_explanation: Manual reconnection does not solve the underlying coverage problem and disrupts mobile use.
reference_notes: CompTIA objectives 3.1 and 5.4 include wireless surveys, coverage, disassociation, and roaming.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which command-line tool is designed to query DNS servers and display DNS record responses?
answer_b: arp
answer_c: netstat
answer_d: traceroute
correct_explanation: The dig utility sends DNS queries and displays the returned records and response details, making it useful for diagnosing DNS resolution.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. dig is a DNS query and troubleshooting utility.
answer_b_explanation: arp displays or modifies local address-resolution cache information.
answer_c_explanation: netstat displays network connections, listening sockets, and related local statistics.
answer_d_explanation: traceroute discovers the sequence of routed hops toward a destination.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.5 includes dig and nslookup. RFC 1035 defines DNS query and response behavior.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: A technician is mapping connections in a network containing switches from several vendors. Which protocol should the technician prefer to discover directly connected devices and their port information using a vendor-neutral standard?
answer_b: TFTP
answer_c: CDP
answer_d: LLDP
correct_explanation: Link Layer Discovery Protocol is an IEEE standard that allows adjacent devices to advertise identity, port, and capability information across a local link. It is vendor neutral.
answer_a_explanation: NTP synchronizes time and does not discover adjacent network devices.
answer_b_explanation: TFTP transfers files and does not advertise neighbor or port information.
answer_c_explanation: CDP performs neighbor discovery but is associated with a specific vendor rather than being the requested vendor-neutral standard.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. LLDP is the IEEE-standard protocol for vendor-neutral link-layer neighbor discovery.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1AB defines LLDP for station and media-access-control connectivity discovery.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
question_text: A router receives an Ethernet frame, removes the data-link header, examines the destination IP address, decrements the packet's TTL, and selects the next hop. At which OSI layer are these forwarding actions primarily occurring?
answer_b: Transport layer
answer_c: Network layer
answer_d: Session layer
correct_explanation: IP addressing, routed forwarding, next-hop selection, and TTL processing are network-layer functions. The router receives the packet inside a data-link frame but makes the forwarding decision at Layer 3.
answer_a_explanation: The physical layer handles signaling and media transmission rather than IP forwarding decisions.
answer_b_explanation: The transport layer handles end-to-end protocols such as TCP and UDP and their port numbers.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Routing based on an IP destination and updating TTL are network-layer operations.
answer_d_explanation: The session layer manages communication sessions and does not perform routed packet forwarding.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.1 maps routed forwarding to the network layer. IP packet forwarding includes hop-limit or TTL processing.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
question_text: An organization wants Internet clients to connect to one public service address while the actual web servers remain hidden on private networks. The intermediary should terminate client connections and forward approved requests to the internal servers. Which function best meets the requirement?
answer_b: A forward proxy
answer_c: A wireless LAN controller
answer_d: A storage area network
correct_explanation: A reverse proxy accepts connections on behalf of protected origin servers and forwards requests to those servers. It can hide internal server addresses and centralize controls such as TLS termination and request filtering.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. A reverse proxy represents servers to external clients and forwards approved requests to internal origins.
answer_b_explanation: A forward proxy represents clients when they access external services rather than representing internal servers to outside users.
answer_c_explanation: A wireless LAN controller coordinates access points and wireless policy.
answer_d_explanation: A storage area network provides block-storage connectivity rather than application proxying.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.2 includes proxy functions. NIST SP 800-41 Rev. 1 discusses application-proxy firewall behavior.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
question_text: Which statement correctly compares network-attached storage with a storage area network?
answer_a: A NAS normally provides only raw block devices, while a SAN provides shared files through SMB.
answer_b: A NAS commonly provides file-level access, while a SAN commonly provides block-level storage to servers.
answer_c: A NAS is a routing protocol, while a SAN is a wireless security protocol.
answer_d: A NAS requires Internet connectivity, while a SAN cannot operate on a private network.
correct_explanation: Network-attached storage exposes shared files through file protocols. A storage area network provides block-storage resources that servers typically treat like locally attached disks.
answer_a_explanation: The access models are reversed. File-level access is associated with NAS, while block-level access is associated with SANs.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. NAS commonly supplies shared files, and SANs commonly present block storage to servers.
answer_c_explanation: Both terms describe storage architectures rather than routing or wireless protocols.
answer_d_explanation: Both NAS and SAN solutions can operate entirely within private organizational networks.
reference_notes: The SNIA Dictionary distinguishes network-attached file storage from block-oriented storage networking.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for predictable private cloud connectivity.
question_text: A financial company must connect its data center to a cloud virtual network. It needs predictable bandwidth, lower variability than an Internet VPN, and a private provider connection that does not traverse the public Internet. Which option best meets the requirement?
answer_a: A clientless remote-access VPN used through employee browsers
answer_b: A public web proxy with content filtering
answer_c: A DNS forwarding rule between the environments
answer_d: A dedicated direct cloud connection through the provider or a connectivity partner
correct_explanation: A dedicated direct connection provides private connectivity into a cloud provider network with more predictable capacity and path characteristics than an encrypted tunnel carried over the public Internet.
answer_a_explanation: Clientless VPN access is designed for individual users and selected applications, not a dedicated data-center interconnect.
answer_b_explanation: A proxy intermediates application requests and does not create private routed connectivity between networks.
answer_c_explanation: DNS forwarding supports name resolution but does not provide a data path between the data center and cloud network.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. A dedicated direct connection is intended for private, predictable cloud connectivity.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.3 compares VPN and direct-connectivity options for cloud networks.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
question_text: Which TWO statements correctly match a network service with its commonly assigned transport port?
answer_a: DHCP servers commonly listen on UDP port 67.
answer_b: NTP commonly uses TCP port 443.
answer_c: NTP commonly uses UDP port 123.
answer_d: DHCP clients commonly listen on TCP port 25.
correct_explanation: DHCP uses UDP ports 67 and 68 for server and client communication. Network Time Protocol commonly uses UDP port 123.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. DHCP server traffic is commonly associated with UDP port 67.
answer_b_explanation: TCP port 443 is commonly used for HTTPS rather than standard NTP.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. NTP commonly uses UDP port 123.
answer_d_explanation: TCP port 25 is commonly associated with SMTP. DHCP clients commonly use UDP port 68.
reference_notes: IANA and the relevant RFCs identify DHCP server UDP 67, DHCP client UDP 68, and NTP UDP 123.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers.
question_text: Which twisted-pair cable category is designed to support 10GBASE-T Ethernet over the standard 100-meter channel length?
answer_b: Category 6A
answer_c: RG-6
answer_d: OS2
correct_explanation: Category 6A is designed to support 10GBASE-T over a 100-meter balanced twisted-pair channel.
answer_a_explanation: Category 3 is an older twisted-pair category and is not designed for 10GBASE-T at 100 meters.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Category 6A supports 10-gigabit Ethernet over the standard 100-meter channel.
answer_c_explanation: RG-6 is coaxial cable rather than balanced twisted-pair Ethernet cabling.
answer_d_explanation: OS2 identifies single-mode optical fiber rather than copper twisted-pair cable.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.5 includes copper cable categories and Ethernet standards. IEEE 802.3 defines 10GBASE-T.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use appropriate IPv4 network addressing.
question_text: A Windows workstation is configured for DHCP but cannot contact a DHCP server. It assigns itself the address 169.254.44.18 with a 16-bit prefix. What type of address is this?
answer_a: A public IPv4 address assigned by the ISP
answer_b: A loopback address
answer_c: A private address from RFC 1918
answer_d: An IPv4 link-local address commonly associated with APIPA
correct_explanation: The 169.254.0.0/16 range is reserved for IPv4 link-local addressing. Systems may self-assign an address from this range when normal address configuration is unavailable.
answer_a_explanation: The 169.254.0.0/16 range is not globally routed public address space.
answer_b_explanation: IPv4 loopback addresses are in 127.0.0.0/8.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The address is an IPv4 link-local address commonly produced by APIPA behavior.
reference_notes: RFC 3927 defines dynamic configuration of IPv4 link-local addresses in 169.254.0.0/16.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: A Layer 2 switch carries VLANs 10, 20, and 30 across one 802.1Q trunk to a router. The router must provide a separate default gateway for each VLAN through that one physical interface. Which router configuration is required?
answer_a: One loopback interface for each access switch
answer_b: One static default route for each VLAN
answer_c: One tagged subinterface with an IP address for each VLAN
answer_d: One DHCP relay configured on the physical interface without VLAN tags
correct_explanation: Router-on-a-stick uses logical subinterfaces on one physical router interface. Each subinterface is associated with an 802.1Q VLAN and receives an IP address that can serve as that VLAN's gateway.
answer_a_explanation: Loopback interfaces are logical router addresses but do not terminate the tagged VLAN trunk for client gateways.
answer_b_explanation: Default routes determine where unknown destinations are forwarded and do not create interfaces for each VLAN.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Tagged subinterfaces allow one physical router link to route for multiple VLANs.
answer_d_explanation: A DHCP relay forwards address requests but does not create separate routed VLAN interfaces.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.1 includes subinterfaces. IEEE 802.1Q defines VLAN tagging used on the trunk.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: An IP phone connects to a switch port, and a user's computer connects through the phone. Voice traffic must be placed in VLAN 40 while the computer remains in data VLAN 20. Which switch-port configuration best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Configure the port with data VLAN 20 and a separate voice VLAN 40.
answer_b: Place all traffic into VLAN 40 and remove the data VLAN.
answer_c: Configure the port as a routed Layer 3 interface with no VLAN membership.
answer_d: Assign the port only to the native VLAN of an unrelated trunk.
correct_explanation: A voice-VLAN configuration allows the phone to tag voice traffic for the voice VLAN while the attached computer's data traffic remains in the configured access VLAN.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The port can support a data access VLAN and a distinct voice VLAN.
answer_b_explanation: This would combine voice and user data rather than segmenting them as required.
answer_c_explanation: A routed port does not provide the access and voice VLAN behavior required for the phone and attached computer.
answer_d_explanation: A native VLAN setting on an unrelated trunk does not create the requested voice and data separation.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.2 includes data and voice VLANs.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_text: When nearby access points provide overlapping 2.4 GHz coverage, which channel-planning approach best reduces interference between the cells?
answer_a: Assign every access point the same channel at maximum power.
answer_b: Assign neighboring access points different non-overlapping channels after a site survey.
answer_c: Disable all channel selection and allow clients to choose a channel.
answer_d: Use wider channels on every access point regardless of nearby networks.
correct_explanation: Neighboring cells should be planned with non-overlapping channels when possible. A site survey helps account for existing use, signal levels, and cell overlap.
answer_a_explanation: Using the same channel on adjacent cells can increase contention and co-channel interference.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Non-overlapping channel assignments reduce interference between nearby cells.
answer_c_explanation: Access points, not clients, select the channel on which the basic service set operates.
answer_d_explanation: Wider channels consume more spectrum and can increase overlap in crowded 2.4 GHz environments.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 includes channel selection, channel width, frequency bands, and wireless surveys.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_text: A wireless network has many dual-band clients crowding the 2.4 GHz band even though 5 GHz coverage is strong. Which feature can encourage compatible clients to use the less-congested 5 GHz band?
answer_b: DHCP relay
answer_c: Spanning tree
answer_d: Band steering
correct_explanation: Band steering attempts to guide capable clients toward a preferred frequency band, commonly moving dual-band clients away from a congested 2.4 GHz band when suitable higher-frequency coverage is available.
answer_a_explanation: Port mirroring copies switch traffic for monitoring and does not influence wireless band selection.
answer_b_explanation: DHCP relay forwards address-assignment traffic across routed boundaries.
answer_c_explanation: Spanning tree prevents Layer 2 loops and does not steer wireless clients between frequency bands.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Band steering encourages capable clients to associate on a preferred band.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 specifically includes band steering.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
question_text: A three-story office has one room where the service-provider handoff, core switches, and building backbone terminate. Each floor also has a smaller room containing access switches and horizontal cabling for that floor. What are these rooms?
answer_a: The central room is an IDF, and each floor room is an MDF.
answer_b: All rooms are screened subnets.
answer_c: The central room is the MDF, and each floor room is an IDF.
answer_d: The central room is a cold site, and each floor room is a warm site.
correct_explanation: The main distribution frame is the primary building telecommunications space and commonly contains the service entrance and core distribution. Intermediate distribution frames serve local floors or areas and connect back to the MDF.
answer_a_explanation: The roles are reversed. The central building distribution room is the MDF.
answer_b_explanation: A screened subnet is a logical security zone rather than a telecommunications room.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The MDF is the main building distribution point, and IDFs distribute connectivity to local areas or floors.
answer_d_explanation: Cold and warm sites are disaster-recovery facilities, not normal building wiring spaces.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.4 includes MDF and IDF placement and physical installation considerations.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
question_text: A 120 V, 20 A circuit is limited by policy to 80% continuous utilization. A rack contains eight 90 W switches and two 450 W servers. Based only on the stated loads, how much capacity remains before reaching the policy limit?
correct_explanation: The policy limit is 120 V multiplied by 20 A multiplied by 0.80, which equals 1,920 W. The equipment load is eight times 90 W plus two times 450 W, which equals 1,620 W. The remaining capacity is 300 W.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. 1,920 W allowed minus 1,620 W used leaves 300 W.
answer_b_explanation: This does not match the difference between the stated policy limit and the equipment load.
answer_c_explanation: This is larger than the remaining capacity after both server and switch loads are included.
answer_d_explanation: This is the equipment load itself, not the unused capacity.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 120 × 20 × 0.80 = 1,920 W; 8 × 90 + 2 × 450 = 1,620 W; remaining capacity = 300 W.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
question_text: Which document should an administrator consult to understand VLANs, IP subnets, routing relationships, and logical network boundaries without focusing on rack positions or cable paths?
answer_b: A logical network diagram
answer_c: A cable plant map
answer_d: A power distribution schedule
correct_explanation: A logical network diagram represents relationships such as subnets, VLANs, routing, and logical security or service boundaries.
answer_a_explanation: A rack elevation shows the physical position of equipment in a rack.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. A logical diagram focuses on network relationships rather than physical placement.
answer_c_explanation: A cable plant map documents physical cabling routes and terminations.
answer_d_explanation: A power schedule documents electrical distribution rather than network topology.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.1 distinguishes logical diagrams from physical documentation.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
question_text: A company wants a carrier contract to state the promised monthly availability, maximum response time for a critical outage, and service credits if the provider misses those commitments. Which document should contain these terms?
answer_b: A packet capture
answer_c: A routing table
answer_d: A service-level agreement
correct_explanation: A service-level agreement documents measurable service commitments such as availability, response times, restoration targets, responsibilities, and remedies.
answer_a_explanation: A rack elevation shows physical equipment placement.
answer_b_explanation: A packet capture records observed network traffic and does not define contractual service commitments.
answer_c_explanation: A routing table contains forwarding information rather than provider performance terms.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The SLA defines measurable service expectations and remedies.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.1 includes service-level agreements as an organizational process and documentation requirement.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: An alert reports that a WAN link is using 75% of its capacity. The operations team does not know whether this is unusual because no historical measurements were retained. What would have been most useful for interpreting the alert?
answer_a: A documented performance baseline for comparable days and times
answer_b: A list of employee vacation requests
answer_c: A physical key inventory for the wiring closet
answer_d: A certificate revocation list
correct_explanation: A performance baseline establishes normal utilization and behavior over time. The current measurement can then be compared with expected patterns to determine whether it represents an anomaly.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Historical baseline data provides context for deciding whether 75% utilization is normal or abnormal.
answer_b_explanation: Vacation requests do not directly establish expected WAN utilization.
answer_c_explanation: A physical key inventory supports access control but does not provide performance context.
answer_d_explanation: A certificate revocation list identifies invalid certificates and does not describe network utilization.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.2 includes baselines, anomaly alerting, and performance monitoring.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
question_text: Which disaster-recovery site normally offers the shortest service-restoration time because systems, connectivity, and current or near-current data are maintained ready for use?
answer_b: A records archive
answer_c: A hot site
answer_d: An empty leased office
correct_explanation: A hot site maintains operational infrastructure and connectivity so services can be restored quickly. It is generally more expensive than warm or cold alternatives because more resources are continuously maintained.
answer_a_explanation: A cold site generally provides space and basic facilities but requires substantial equipment and data restoration before use.
answer_b_explanation: A records archive stores information but is not an operational recovery environment.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A hot site is maintained at the highest readiness level for rapid recovery.
answer_d_explanation: An empty office lacks the systems and connectivity described.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 discusses alternate processing sites and recovery readiness.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
question_text: IPv6 clients on a LAN should create their own addresses from the advertised network prefix without receiving address assignments from a stateful DHCPv6 server. Which mechanism provides this behavior?
answer_b: SLAAC using router advertisements
answer_c: ARP
answer_d: IPv4 APIPA
correct_explanation: Stateless Address Autoconfiguration allows an IPv6 host to form an address using information advertised by a local router, including the network prefix.
answer_a_explanation: NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4 communication and does not assign local IPv6 addresses.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. SLAAC uses router advertisements to provide prefix and configuration information.
answer_c_explanation: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to link-layer addresses and is not used for IPv6 address assignment.
answer_d_explanation: APIPA refers to IPv4 link-local self-assignment and does not configure a routable IPv6 prefix.
reference_notes: RFC 4862 defines IPv6 Stateless Address Autoconfiguration.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Compare and contrast network access and management methods.
question_text: Two branch networks need persistent encrypted connectivity so hosts at either site can reach approved resources at the other site without individual users launching VPN clients. Which solution is most appropriate?
answer_a: A clientless browser portal for each user
answer_b: A local hosts file copied to every workstation
answer_c: A wireless guest network
answer_d: A site-to-site VPN between the network gateways
correct_explanation: A site-to-site VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between network gateways. Traffic for the remote network can enter the tunnel automatically according to routing and security policy.
answer_a_explanation: A clientless portal provides selected application access for users rather than persistent network-to-network connectivity.
answer_b_explanation: A hosts file affects local name resolution and does not encrypt or route traffic between sites.
answer_c_explanation: A guest wireless network does not provide protected branch-to-branch connectivity.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. A gateway-to-gateway site-to-site VPN joins approved network traffic across the untrusted path.
reference_notes: RFC 4301 defines IPsec security architecture used for protected network-layer tunnels.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Which TWO combinations use two different authentication-factor categories?
answer_a: A password and a hardware security token
answer_b: A password and a personal identification number
answer_c: A smart card and a one-time-password token
answer_d: A fingerprint and a password
correct_explanation: A password is a knowledge factor, a hardware token is a possession factor, and a fingerprint is an inherence factor. Password plus token and fingerprint plus password each combine distinct factor categories.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. This combines something the user knows with something the user possesses.
answer_b_explanation: A password and a PIN are both knowledge factors, so the combination is not multifactor by itself.
answer_c_explanation: A smart card and a hardware one-time-password token are both possession factors.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. This combines an inherence factor with a knowledge factor.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-63B defines authentication factors and multifactor authentication.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Which standard is commonly used to exchange signed authentication assertions between an identity provider and browser-based service providers for federated single sign-on?
answer_b: SAML
answer_c: LACP
answer_d: TFTP
correct_explanation: Security Assertion Markup Language allows an identity provider to send authentication and related assertions to a service provider, supporting federated browser-based single sign-on.
answer_a_explanation: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to local link-layer addresses.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. SAML exchanges identity assertions between identity and service providers.
answer_c_explanation: LACP negotiates bundled Ethernet links.
answer_d_explanation: TFTP transfers files and does not provide identity federation.
reference_notes: The OASIS SAML 2.0 specifications define assertions and protocols used between identity and service providers.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: A public service becomes unavailable after thousands of compromised systems across many networks simultaneously send high volumes of requests. Which attack best describes the event?
answer_b: ARP poisoning
answer_c: Distributed denial of service
answer_d: Password spraying
correct_explanation: A distributed denial-of-service attack uses many distributed sources to overwhelm a service or its supporting network resources.
answer_a_explanation: VLAN hopping attempts to reach traffic in another VLAN and does not describe distributed service exhaustion.
answer_b_explanation: ARP poisoning manipulates local address-resolution information and is not the high-volume distributed attack described.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Many compromised systems are coordinating traffic to deny availability.
answer_d_explanation: Password spraying tests common passwords across accounts and does not primarily exhaust network capacity.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.2 includes DoS and DDoS attacks. NIST SP 800-94 discusses monitoring network attacks and traffic anomalies.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for restricting an access port to one expected endpoint.
question_text: A switch port in a public conference room should permit one approved device. The switch should learn that device's MAC address, retain it as the allowed address, and disable the port if a different device appears. Which feature best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Port security with a maximum of one sticky MAC address and a shutdown violation action
answer_b: A trunk native-VLAN change
answer_c: A DHCP relay on the switch interface
answer_d: A larger spanning-tree bridge priority
correct_explanation: Port security can restrict the number or identity of source MAC addresses learned on an access port. Sticky learning can retain the approved address, and a shutdown action can disable the port after a violation.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The stated port-security settings match the learning, retention, and violation requirements.
answer_b_explanation: A native-VLAN setting affects untagged trunk traffic and does not restrict the endpoint MAC address.
answer_c_explanation: A DHCP relay forwards address-assignment messages and does not enforce one approved endpoint.
answer_d_explanation: Spanning-tree priority influences root-bridge selection and does not provide endpoint authorization.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.3 includes port security, MAC filtering, and device-hardening controls.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
question_text: A technician tests the most likely theory for a network outage, but the test shows that the suspected component is operating correctly. According to the troubleshooting methodology, what should the technician do next?
answer_a: Establish a new theory of probable cause or escalate based on the available evidence.
answer_b: Document the issue as resolved without further testing.
answer_c: Implement the original fix even though the theory was disproven.
answer_d: Skip directly to preventive measures without identifying the cause.
correct_explanation: When a theory is not confirmed, the technician should develop another probable cause or escalate when appropriate. The process should continue from the evidence rather than implementing an unsupported change.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. A disproven theory leads to another theory or an appropriate escalation.
answer_b_explanation: The service has not been restored or verified, so the issue cannot be closed.
answer_c_explanation: Implementing a fix based on a disproven cause can introduce risk without resolving the outage.
answer_d_explanation: Preventive measures follow a verified solution rather than replacing root-cause analysis.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.1 directs technicians to establish a new theory or escalate when the current theory is not confirmed.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A newly installed duplex fiber link shows no carrier at either end. The transceivers and fiber type match, and optical power is present on each transmitter. Inspection shows that the transmit strand on each end connects to the remote transmit port. What should the technician do?
answer_b: Swap one end of the duplex pair so transmit connects to receive.
answer_c: Configure a DHCP relay on the interface.
answer_d: Change the DNS server address.
correct_explanation: A duplex fiber link requires the transmitter on each device to connect to the receiver on the other device. If transmit connects to transmit, neither receiver obtains the remote signal.
answer_a_explanation: MTU configuration does not correct physical fiber polarity.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Reversing one duplex pair establishes transmit-to-receive connectivity in both directions.
answer_c_explanation: DHCP relay affects address-assignment traffic and cannot create optical carrier.
answer_d_explanation: DNS settings do not affect the physical fiber link state.
study_topics: Fiber polarity|Transmit and receive|Duplex fiber|Physical troubleshooting
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.2 includes transmit-and-receive transposition and fiber-interface troubleshooting.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: A workstation has address 192.168.10.50, default gateway 192.168.10.1, and mask 255.255.0.0. The intended local subnet is 192.168.10.0/24. The workstation can reach some local hosts but fails when trying to reach 192.168.20.25 because it repeatedly sends ARP requests for that destination instead of forwarding traffic to the gateway. What is the cause?
answer_a: The DNS resolver is using TCP rather than UDP.
answer_b: The gateway has a duplicate MAC address.
answer_c: The workstation's subnet mask is too broad.
answer_d: The destination requires a voice VLAN.
correct_explanation: The /16 mask makes the workstation believe that 192.168.20.25 is on the local link. It therefore attempts ARP instead of sending the packet to the default gateway. The intended /24 mask would classify the destination as remote.
answer_a_explanation: DNS transport does not determine whether the host treats an IPv4 destination as local or remote.
answer_b_explanation: The symptom results from the host not using the gateway at all, not from a duplicate gateway MAC address.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The overly broad mask incorrectly places the remote destination in the local subnet.
answer_d_explanation: Voice VLAN configuration is unrelated to IPv4 subnet classification.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.3 includes incorrect subnet masks. The host applies its prefix to decide whether to resolve a destination locally or send through a gateway.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: A monitoring test sends 9,000 packets and receives 8,955 replies. What percentage of the packets were lost?
correct_explanation: The test lost 9,000 minus 8,955, which equals 45 packets. Dividing 45 by 9,000 and multiplying by 100 gives 0.5% packet loss.
answer_a_explanation: This is one-tenth of the calculated loss percentage.
answer_b_explanation: This does not match 45 losses out of 9,000 transmitted packets.
answer_c_explanation: A 5% loss rate would represent 450 lost packets.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. 45 divided by 9,000 equals 0.005, or 0.5%.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which tool is commonly used to discover hosts and identify open TCP or UDP ports on a network?
answer_b: Nmap
answer_c: An optical power meter
answer_d: A punchdown tool
correct_explanation: Nmap is a network discovery and port-scanning tool that can identify reachable hosts and probe for exposed services.
answer_a_explanation: A tone generator helps trace physical copper cabling.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Nmap is designed for network discovery and port scanning.
answer_c_explanation: An optical power meter measures light levels on fiber links.
answer_d_explanation: A punchdown tool terminates conductors on blocks and jacks.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.5 lists Nmap among command-line and network troubleshooting tools.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Users report that a file-transfer session pauses repeatedly. The administrator needs to verify whether TCP segments are being retransmitted and examine acknowledgments, sequence numbers, and timing. Which tool is most appropriate?
answer_b: A Wi-Fi heat map with no packet capture
answer_c: A protocol analyzer capturing the affected traffic
answer_d: A physical access-control badge reader
correct_explanation: A protocol analyzer can capture and decode TCP traffic, allowing the administrator to inspect retransmissions, acknowledgments, sequence numbers, window behavior, and packet timing.
answer_a_explanation: A rack elevation documents equipment placement and contains no packet-level data.
answer_b_explanation: A heat map can show wireless coverage but does not provide the requested TCP sequence and acknowledgment details.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A packet capture and protocol analyzer provides the transport-layer evidence needed.
answer_d_explanation: A badge reader controls physical access and does not analyze network sessions.
reference_notes: RFC 9293 defines TCP sequence, acknowledgment, and retransmission behavior. CompTIA objective 5.5 includes protocol analyzers and packet capture.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which tool is most appropriate for verifying the pinout, continuity, cable length, and split-pair condition of an installed twisted-pair Ethernet cable?
answer_b: A Wi-Fi analyzer
answer_c: A loopback plug
answer_d: A copper cable tester or certifier
correct_explanation: A copper cable tester or certifier can evaluate wiremap, continuity, length, and pair-related faults such as split pairs. More advanced certifiers can also test performance against a cabling category.
answer_a_explanation: A packet sniffer analyzes network frames and packets after a link operates; it does not verify cable wiremap.
answer_b_explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer measures wireless signal and spectrum conditions.
answer_c_explanation: A loopback plug tests an interface's transmit and receive path but does not certify the installed cable's pair mapping and length.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. A cable tester or certifier directly measures the stated twisted-pair characteristics.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.5 includes cable testers and physical troubleshooting tools.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-25.

objective_text: Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model.
question_text: A server receives an IP packet addressed to one of its interfaces. The operating system examines the TCP destination port to decide whether the payload belongs to the web service, mail service, or another application. Which OSI layer provides this application multiplexing function?
answer_b: Transport layer
answer_c: Network layer
answer_d: Data-link layer
correct_explanation: The transport layer uses port numbers to identify application endpoints. TCP and UDP allow multiple application conversations to share one host IP address while being delivered to the correct process.
answer_a_explanation: The physical layer carries signals and does not identify application processes.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. TCP and UDP port numbers provide transport-layer multiplexing to applications.
answer_c_explanation: The network layer delivers packets to an IP address but does not identify the receiving application by port.
answer_d_explanation: The data-link layer delivers frames on the local network using link-layer addressing.
reference_notes: RFC 9293 and RFC 768 define TCP and UDP port fields used to identify transport endpoints.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions.
question_text: Which technology places cached copies of web content at geographically distributed edge locations to reduce latency and load on the origin servers?
answer_b: A DHCP relay
answer_c: A content delivery network
answer_d: A first-hop redundancy protocol
correct_explanation: A content delivery network distributes and caches content at edge locations closer to users. This can reduce user latency and decrease repeated requests to the origin infrastructure.
answer_a_explanation: A storage area network provides block-storage connectivity to servers.
answer_b_explanation: A DHCP relay forwards address-configuration messages across routed boundaries.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. A CDN uses distributed edge locations to serve cached content.
answer_d_explanation: A first-hop redundancy protocol protects a local default gateway.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.2 includes content delivery networks and their network function.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Summarize cloud concepts and connectivity options.
question_text: A development team uploads application code to a cloud service. The provider manages the operating system, runtime, middleware, and underlying infrastructure, while the team manages its code and application data. Which service model is this?
answer_b: Infrastructure as a service
answer_c: Colocation
answer_d: Platform as a service
correct_explanation: Platform as a service provides a managed application platform, including the runtime and supporting infrastructure. Customers deploy and manage their applications without administering the underlying operating system.
answer_a_explanation: Software as a service delivers a complete provider-managed application to end users.
answer_b_explanation: Infrastructure as a service generally leaves operating-system and runtime management to the customer.
answer_c_explanation: Colocation provides facility space and connectivity for customer-owned equipment rather than a managed application platform.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. PaaS lets the team deploy code onto a provider-managed platform.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-145 defines the platform-as-a-service capability and customer responsibility boundary.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types.
question_text: Which TWO statements correctly identify commonly assigned SNMP transport ports?
answer_a: SNMP agents commonly receive manager requests on UDP port 161.
answer_b: SNMP traps commonly use TCP port 22.
answer_c: SNMP agents commonly receive polling requests on UDP port 53.
answer_d: SNMP managers commonly receive traps or notifications on UDP port 162.
correct_explanation: SNMP requests are commonly sent to an agent on UDP port 161. Traps and similar notifications are commonly delivered to the management system on UDP port 162.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. UDP port 161 is assigned to the SNMP service used for management requests.
answer_b_explanation: TCP port 22 is assigned to SSH rather than SNMP notifications.
answer_c_explanation: UDP port 53 is assigned to DNS service.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. UDP port 162 is assigned to SNMP trap service.
reference_notes: IANA assigns UDP ports 161 and 162 to SNMP and SNMP trap service. RFC 3411 defines the SNMP management framework.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Compare and contrast transmission media and transceivers.
question_text: Which statement best distinguishes a QSFP-family transceiver from an SFP-family transceiver?
answer_a: QSFP form factors commonly provide four data lanes, supporting higher aggregate bandwidth or breakout connections.
answer_b: QSFP modules are used only for copper telephone circuits.
answer_c: SFP modules cannot support optical fiber.
answer_d: QSFP modules remove the need to match wavelength, media type, and supported distance.
correct_explanation: QSFP means quad small form-factor pluggable and commonly uses four data lanes. Depending on the module and equipment, those lanes can provide a higher aggregate rate or be broken out into separate lower-rate links.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Multiple lanes are a key distinction of QSFP-family modules.
answer_b_explanation: QSFP modules are widely used for high-speed Ethernet and optical interconnects, not only telephone circuits.
answer_c_explanation: Many SFP-family modules are optical transceivers.
answer_d_explanation: Media, wavelength, speed, and distance compatibility still matter when selecting a QSFP module.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.5 includes SFP and QSFP transceiver form factors. IEEE 802.3 defines Ethernet physical interfaces using pluggable transceivers.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Summarize evolving use cases for modern network environments.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for a gradual IPv6 migration while maintaining native IPv4 service.
question_text: An organization is introducing IPv6, but many internal and external services still require IPv4. Endpoints and routers should use native IPv6 where available and continue using native IPv4 when required during the transition. Which approach best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Remove IPv4 from every system before enabling IPv6.
answer_b: Encapsulate all Ethernet frames inside GRE regardless of destination protocol.
answer_c: Run IPv4 and IPv6 concurrently using dual stack.
answer_d: Replace IP routing with one extended Layer 2 broadcast domain.
correct_explanation: Dual stack enables devices to operate IPv4 and IPv6 at the same time. Applications and routing can use the protocol appropriate for the destination while the organization migrates services gradually.
answer_a_explanation: Removing IPv4 immediately would break access to services that still require it.
answer_b_explanation: GRE encapsulation is not a general replacement for native IPv4 and IPv6 operation.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Dual stack provides native operation for both protocol versions during transition.
answer_d_explanation: Extending one Layer 2 domain does not replace IP routing or provide an IPv6 migration strategy.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 1.8 includes IPv6 transition mechanisms. Dual stack maintains concurrent native IPv4 and IPv6 operation.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: A router has routes for 10.0.0.0/8 through Router A, 10.20.0.0/16 through Router B, 10.20.30.0/24 through Router C, and 10.20.30.128/25 through Router D. Which next hop will be selected for destination 10.20.30.200?
answer_b: Router B
answer_c: Router C
answer_d: Router D
correct_explanation: The destination matches every listed prefix, but the /25 route has the longest prefix and is therefore the most specific match. The router selects Router D.
answer_a_explanation: The /8 route matches but is less specific than the /16, /24, and /25 routes.
answer_b_explanation: The /16 route is more specific than /8 but less specific than /24 and /25.
answer_c_explanation: The /24 route matches the destination but is less specific than the matching /25 route.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. 10.20.30.200 falls within 10.20.30.128/25, the longest matching prefix.
reference_notes: CIDR forwarding selects the most specific matching prefix when multiple routes cover a destination.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Explain characteristics of routing technologies.
question_text: A router learns the same destination prefix from two different route sources. Before comparing protocol-specific metrics, which value is commonly used to prefer the more trusted route source?
answer_b: Administrative distance
answer_c: Ethernet frame check sequence
answer_d: Wireless channel width
correct_explanation: Administrative distance ranks the trustworthiness of different route sources. When the same prefix is learned from different sources, the route with the preferred administrative distance is selected before comparing metrics within one routing protocol.
answer_a_explanation: A VLAN identifier separates Layer 2 broadcast domains and does not rank route sources.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. Administrative distance is used to compare routes learned through different mechanisms or protocols.
answer_c_explanation: The frame check sequence detects link-layer transmission errors.
answer_d_explanation: Channel width affects wireless spectrum use and not route-source preference.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.1 includes administrative distance and route-selection concepts.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: In a spanning-tree instance, which switch becomes the root bridge?
answer_a: The switch with the highest port count
answer_b: The switch with the highest MAC address
answer_c: The switch with the lowest bridge ID
answer_d: The switch that most recently joined the network
correct_explanation: Spanning tree elects the switch with the lowest bridge ID as the root bridge. The bridge ID incorporates the configured priority and a switch identifier.
answer_a_explanation: Port count is not the root-election criterion.
answer_b_explanation: A higher switch identifier would not produce the lowest bridge ID.
