answer_c_explanation: Correct. The lowest bridge ID wins the root-bridge election.
answer_d_explanation: Join time does not determine the spanning-tree root.
reference_notes: IEEE 802.1Q bridged-network standards define spanning-tree root selection using the bridge identifier.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Given a scenario, configure switching technologies and features.
question_text: VLANs 10, 20, and 30 span two switches connected by an 802.1Q trunk. Devices in VLANs 10 and 20 communicate across the trunk, but VLAN 30 devices cannot. The access ports and VLAN 30 database entries are correct on both switches. What should the administrator check next?
answer_a: Whether VLAN 30 is permitted on the trunk's allowed-VLAN list
answer_b: Whether the DHCP server uses a longer lease time
answer_c: Whether the switches have matching NTP strata
answer_d: Whether the access points use directional antennas
correct_explanation: A trunk can be configured to carry only selected VLANs. If VLAN 30 is missing from the allowed list, its tagged frames will not cross the trunk even though the VLAN and access ports exist on both switches.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. An omitted allowed VLAN explains why only VLAN 30 fails across the trunk.
answer_b_explanation: DHCP lease time does not control whether tagged VLAN frames cross a switch trunk.
answer_c_explanation: NTP configuration affects time synchronization rather than VLAN forwarding.
answer_d_explanation: Wireless antenna selection is unrelated to the wired trunk issue.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.2 includes 802.1Q trunking and VLAN configuration.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Given a scenario, select and configure wireless devices and technologies.
question_instruction: Select the BEST answer for providing visitor Internet access while protecting internal systems.
question_text: A company wants guests to connect to Wi-Fi, accept usage terms through a web page, reach the Internet, and remain isolated from employee networks and other guest clients. Which design best meets the requirement?
answer_a: Place guests on the employee VLAN and rely only on the SSID name.
answer_b: Disable encryption and bridge the guest SSID directly to the server VLAN.
answer_c: Give guests the internal pre-shared key and allow unrestricted east-west traffic.
answer_d: Use a dedicated guest SSID and VLAN with a captive portal, client isolation, and firewall rules permitting only required Internet access.
correct_explanation: A separate guest network limits access to internal resources. A captive portal can present terms or authentication, client isolation limits direct guest-to-guest traffic, and firewall policy can restrict the network to approved Internet access.
answer_a_explanation: An SSID name does not create security isolation from the employee network.
answer_b_explanation: Bridging guests to a server VLAN would expose protected resources.
answer_c_explanation: Sharing internal credentials and allowing east-west traffic conflicts with the isolation requirement.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. The dedicated guest design provides segmentation, controlled onboarding, and restricted access.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 2.3 includes guest networks and captive portals. Firewall zoning provides separation from trusted networks.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Explain important factors of physical installations.
question_text: A 42U rack contains eight switches that each occupy 2U and ten patch panels that each occupy 1U. Ignoring spacing and other equipment, how many rack units remain available?
correct_explanation: The switches use 8 multiplied by 2U, which equals 16U. The patch panels use 10 multiplied by 1U, which equals 10U. The total used space is 26U, leaving 42U minus 26U, or 16U.
answer_a_explanation: This understates the remaining rack capacity.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. 42U minus 16U of switches and 10U of patch panels leaves 16U.
answer_c_explanation: This ignores part of the installed equipment.
answer_d_explanation: This is the amount of rack space already occupied, not the remaining space.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 42 - (8 × 2) - (10 × 1) = 16 rack units.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures.
question_text: Why should an organization track the end-of-support date for network devices?
answer_a: To plan replacement before security updates, technical assistance, or replacement support become unavailable
answer_b: To determine the wireless channel used by every access point
answer_c: To calculate the checksum of every Ethernet frame
answer_d: To select the DNS record for an email server
correct_explanation: End-of-support tracking helps the organization replace or mitigate aging devices before vendor updates, fixes, parts, or technical assistance are no longer available.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Lifecycle tracking supports planned replacement and risk management.
answer_b_explanation: Wireless channel selection is an operational configuration task rather than the purpose of end-of-support tracking.
answer_c_explanation: Frame checksums are generated and checked by network interfaces.
answer_d_explanation: Email routing uses DNS records such as MX and is unrelated to device lifecycle.
study_topics: End of support|Lifecycle management|Asset inventory|Replacement planning
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.1 includes end-of-life, end-of-support, and software-management lifecycle concepts.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: A switch configuration changes at 2:00 a.m., but there is no approved change ticket. The operations team wants an automated alert whenever a device differs from its approved configuration. Which monitoring capability is most appropriate?
answer_b: Cable qualification
answer_c: Configuration monitoring that compares devices with an approved baseline
answer_d: DNS recursion testing
correct_explanation: Configuration monitoring can collect or compare device configurations against an approved baseline. Unexpected differences can be flagged as configuration drift or an unauthorized change.
answer_a_explanation: A heat map measures wireless coverage and signal conditions.
answer_b_explanation: Cable qualification evaluates physical media performance.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Baseline comparison identifies configuration drift and unapproved changes.
answer_d_explanation: DNS recursion testing evaluates name-resolution behavior, not device configuration state.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use network monitoring technologies.
question_text: A monitoring platform should detect when a public application stops responding even if the server remains powered on and its network interface stays up. Which check provides the most useful evidence?
answer_b: A synthetic request that connects to the application and verifies an expected response
answer_c: A list of switch serial numbers
answer_d: A static cable label database
correct_explanation: A synthetic availability check exercises the service from the user's perspective. It can detect application, protocol, or dependency failures that a simple interface-up check would miss.
answer_a_explanation: A rack-door sensor indicates physical access but not application availability.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. An end-to-end service request verifies that the application responds as expected.
answer_c_explanation: Serial numbers support inventory management and do not measure live availability.
answer_d_explanation: Cable labels document infrastructure but do not test the service.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
question_text: Which TWO statements correctly describe common reliability and repair metrics?
answer_a: MTTR estimates the average operating time between one failure and the next.
answer_b: MTBF estimates the average operating time between failures for a repairable system.
answer_c: MTBF specifies the maximum amount of data that may be lost after an incident.
answer_d: MTTR estimates the average time required to repair or restore a failed system.
correct_explanation: Mean time between failures measures average operating time between failures for a repairable system. Mean time to repair measures average repair or restoration duration.
answer_a_explanation: This describes MTBF rather than MTTR.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. MTBF is an average time-between-failures measure.
answer_c_explanation: Maximum tolerable data loss is addressed by the recovery point objective, not MTBF.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. MTTR measures average repair or restoration time.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 3.3 includes MTTR and MTBF. NIST contingency-planning guidance discusses restoration and recovery metrics.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts.
question_text: Leaders from networking, security, facilities, and business operations meet to walk through a simulated data-center outage. They discuss decisions, communication paths, responsibilities, and gaps without interrupting production systems. What type of exercise is this?
answer_b: A destructive failover test
answer_c: A packet-capture replay
answer_d: A cable certification test
correct_explanation: A tabletop exercise is a discussion-based review of a simulated incident. Participants evaluate plans, roles, decisions, and communication without performing a full operational disruption.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The participants are discussing a scenario and validating procedures without a live failover.
answer_b_explanation: A destructive or full operational test would involve actual systems and greater production impact.
answer_c_explanation: Packet replay is a technical traffic-analysis activity rather than an organizational recovery exercise.
answer_d_explanation: Cable certification validates physical cabling performance.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 describes discussion-based and operational contingency-plan testing.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services.
question_text: Which technology allows a validating resolver to verify the origin and integrity of signed DNS data but does not by itself encrypt the DNS query?
answer_b: DNSSEC
answer_c: NAT64
answer_d: LACP
correct_explanation: DNS Security Extensions use digital signatures to authenticate DNS data and detect modification. DNSSEC does not provide confidentiality for the query and response traffic.
answer_a_explanation: SLAAC configures IPv6 addresses and does not authenticate DNS data.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. DNSSEC provides data-origin authentication and integrity validation.
answer_c_explanation: NAT64 translates between IPv6 clients and IPv4 services.
answer_d_explanation: LACP negotiates Ethernet link aggregation.
reference_notes: RFC 4033 introduces DNSSEC authentication and integrity services and explains that confidentiality is outside its scope.

objective_text: Explain the importance of basic network security concepts.
question_text: Two workloads are on the same virtual network, but policy should allow one specific application flow between them and deny other east-west connections. Which security approach most directly meets the requirement?
answer_a: Place every workload in one unrestricted trust zone.
answer_b: Increase the Internet circuit bandwidth.
answer_c: Disable all logging between virtual machines.
answer_d: Apply microsegmentation policies between the workloads.
correct_explanation: Microsegmentation applies granular policy between workloads, even when they share broader network infrastructure. It can restrict east-west movement to explicitly permitted flows.
answer_a_explanation: One unrestricted zone would allow more lateral communication than required.
answer_b_explanation: Additional bandwidth does not enforce workload-to-workload access policy.
answer_c_explanation: Disabling logs reduces visibility and does not create segmentation.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. Microsegmentation provides fine-grained controls between individual workloads or groups.
reference_notes: NIST SP 800-207 supports granular policy enforcement and limiting implicit trust between resources.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: Which attack sends many frames with different forged source MAC addresses in an attempt to overflow a switch's forwarding table?
answer_b: DNS cache poisoning
answer_c: Evil twin
answer_d: Password spraying
correct_explanation: A MAC-flooding attack attempts to fill a switch's MAC address table with forged entries. Depending on the switch behavior, this can disrupt forwarding or cause traffic to be flooded more broadly.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. The attack targets the switch's MAC or content-addressable-memory table.
answer_b_explanation: DNS cache poisoning inserts false name-resolution information.
answer_c_explanation: An evil twin is a fraudulent wireless access point.
answer_d_explanation: Password spraying tests a small set of passwords against many accounts.
study_topics: MAC flooding|Switch forwarding table|Layer 2 attack|CAM table
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.2 includes MAC flooding as a network attack.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network.
question_text: Users enter the correct name for a banking website, but an internal resolver returns an attacker-controlled IP address because a forged record was inserted into its cache. Which attack occurred?
answer_b: MAC flooding
answer_c: DNS cache poisoning
answer_d: Wireless deauthentication
correct_explanation: DNS cache poisoning places false resource-record information into a resolver's cache. Clients relying on that resolver can then be directed to an incorrect address despite entering the correct name.
answer_a_explanation: VLAN hopping attempts to cross Layer 2 segmentation and does not alter DNS answers.
answer_b_explanation: MAC flooding targets a switch forwarding table.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The resolver cache contains a forged mapping for the legitimate name.
answer_d_explanation: Wireless deauthentication disrupts client associations and does not change DNS records.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 4.2 includes DNS poisoning and spoofing. DNSSEC is designed to help validators detect forged signed DNS data.
author_notes: Accelerated staging approval authorized by the repository owner on 2026-07-26.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_text: Which security control blocks web requests according to destination addresses, domain names, or site categories such as malware and phishing?
answer_b: URL filtering
answer_c: Route summarization
answer_d: Spanning tree
correct_explanation: URL filtering evaluates requested web destinations and applies policy based on specific addresses, domains, reputation, or content categories.
answer_a_explanation: Link aggregation combines physical links for capacity and redundancy.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. URL filtering applies policy to requested web destinations.
answer_c_explanation: Route summarization combines prefixes in a routing table.
answer_d_explanation: Spanning tree prevents Layer 2 loops.

objective_text: Given a scenario, apply network security features, defense techniques, and solutions.
question_text: An administrator confirms that the private key for a network appliance's TLS certificate was copied by an unauthorized party. Which response best addresses the cryptographic compromise?
answer_a: Keep the current certificate until its normal expiration date.
answer_b: Change only the appliance's DNS name.
answer_c: Revoke the certificate, generate a new key pair, and obtain a replacement certificate.
answer_d: Increase the appliance's Ethernet MTU.
correct_explanation: A compromised private key can no longer be trusted. The associated certificate should be revoked, a new key pair should be generated, and a new certificate should be issued for the replacement public key.
answer_a_explanation: Continuing to use the compromised key leaves the service vulnerable to impersonation or decryption risks.
answer_b_explanation: Changing a DNS name does not invalidate or replace the exposed private key.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. Revocation and replacement with a new key pair restore a trustworthy certificate binding.
answer_d_explanation: MTU configuration has no effect on certificate or key compromise.
reference_notes: RFC 5280 defines certificate revocation information and certification-path validation.

objective_text: Explain the troubleshooting methodology.
question_text: A technician has confirmed that an incorrect routing policy caused an outage. Before changing the production router, what should the technician do according to the troubleshooting methodology?
answer_a: Create a plan of action that considers potential effects and includes an appropriate rollback or escalation path.
answer_b: Delete all configuration backups to avoid confusion.
answer_c: Change several unrelated settings at the same time.
answer_d: Close the incident before implementing the correction.
correct_explanation: After confirming the cause, the technician should plan the corrective action and consider its possible effects. The plan should account for risk, approval, rollback, and escalation as appropriate.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. Planning reduces the chance that the fix creates a wider outage and provides a recovery path.
answer_b_explanation: Configuration backups support rollback and should not be deleted.
answer_c_explanation: Multiple unrelated changes make results harder to evaluate and add risk.
answer_d_explanation: The incident remains unresolved until the change is implemented and verified.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.1 includes establishing a plan of action and identifying potential effects.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A twisted-pair Ethernet link is stable at a short temporary cable length but becomes intermittent when connected through a 135-meter permanent run. Terminations test correctly and there is no strong electromagnetic interference. What is the most likely cause?
answer_b: Excessive cable length causing signal attenuation
answer_c: A missing default route
answer_d: An expired TLS certificate
correct_explanation: A 135-meter copper Ethernet channel exceeds the common 100-meter channel limit for twisted-pair Ethernet. Excessive attenuation and signal degradation can cause errors or link instability.
answer_a_explanation: DNS zone configuration does not affect the physical Ethernet signal.
answer_b_explanation: Correct. The permanent run is beyond the normal copper Ethernet channel distance.
answer_c_explanation: A missing route affects Layer 3 reachability but does not make the physical link intermittent.
answer_d_explanation: A certificate issue affects authenticated applications rather than Ethernet carrier quality.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.2 includes signal degradation and incorrect cable selection. Ethernet standards define supported channel characteristics.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues.
question_text: A technician installs a 10 GbE optical transceiver into a switch port that supports only 1 GbE modules. The fiber type and connector are correct, but the link remains down. What is the most likely cause?
answer_a: The DNS server has an incorrect PTR record.
answer_b: The client has an exhausted DHCP lease.
answer_c: The transceiver speed is not supported by the switch port.
answer_d: The switch has the wrong NTP time source.
correct_explanation: A transceiver must be supported by the device and port at the required speed. Matching fiber and connectors is not sufficient when the port cannot operate with the installed module.
answer_a_explanation: A PTR record affects reverse name resolution and not the physical link state.
answer_b_explanation: DHCP addressing occurs after a working link is established.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The module and port have incompatible supported speeds.
answer_d_explanation: NTP configuration does not determine transceiver compatibility.
reference_notes: CompTIA objective 5.2 includes transceiver mismatch and interface status troubleshooting.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services.
question_text: Existing users retain network connectivity, but newly connected clients cannot obtain an IPv4 lease. The DHCP server is reachable, and its log reports that no addresses are available in the scope. What is the cause?
answer_b: A DNSSEC validation failure
answer_c: An exhausted DHCP address pool
answer_d: A fiber transmit-and-receive reversal
correct_explanation: The server has no unused addresses available to lease. Existing clients can continue using valid leases, while new clients fail until addresses expire, the pool is expanded, or unused leases are reclaimed.
answer_a_explanation: Spanning-tree root selection would not produce a server log stating that the address pool is empty.
answer_b_explanation: DNSSEC validation does not assign IPv4 addresses.
answer_c_explanation: Correct. The DHCP scope has no available leases for new clients.
answer_d_explanation: A fiber polarity fault would disrupt the underlying link rather than selectively affect new address requests.
reference_notes: RFC 2131 defines DHCP address allocation and lease behavior. CompTIA objective 5.3 includes address-pool issues.

objective_text: Given a scenario, troubleshoot common performance issues.
question_text: A 2.5 GB file, using decimal units, crosses a path whose slowest link is 200 Mbps. Ignoring protocol overhead and other traffic, what is the theoretical minimum transfer time?
answer_b: 10 seconds
answer_c: 1,000 seconds
answer_d: 12.5 seconds
correct_explanation: The file contains 2.5 billion bytes, or 20 billion bits. Dividing 20 billion bits by 200 million bits per second gives 100 seconds. The slowest path link limits the theoretical throughput.
answer_a_explanation: Correct. 2.5 GB multiplied by 8 equals 20 Gb, and 20 Gb divided by 0.2 Gbps equals 100 seconds.
answer_b_explanation: Ten seconds would require a 2 Gbps effective path.
answer_c_explanation: One thousand seconds is ten times the calculated ideal transfer time.
answer_d_explanation: This result does not convert the full file from bytes to bits before dividing by the link rate.
reference_notes: Programmatic check: 2.5 × 10^9 bytes × 8 / (200 × 10^6 bits per second) = 100 seconds.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which command is commonly used to test IP reachability and measure round-trip response time by sending ICMP echo requests?
answer_b: arp
answer_c: netstat
answer_d: ping
correct_explanation: The ping command sends ICMP echo requests and reports whether replies are received, commonly including round-trip timing and loss information.

answer_b_explanation: arp displays or changes local address-resolution cache information.
answer_c_explanation: netstat displays network connections and socket information.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. ping uses ICMP echo messages to test reachability and timing.

objective_text: Given a scenario, use the appropriate tool or protocol to solve networking issues.
question_text: Which command-line utility is most appropriate for listing local listening sockets and established network connections on a host?
answer_b: A time-domain reflectometer

answer_d: netstat or ss
correct_explanation: The netstat and ss utilities display local socket information, including listening ports, established connections, addresses, and protocol state.

answer_b_explanation: A time-domain reflectometer locates faults in copper cabling.
answer_c_explanation: A Wi-Fi analyzer evaluates wireless spectrum and signal conditions.
answer_d_explanation: Correct. netstat and ss provide local connection and listening-socket information.
